title: Interfacial gap formation in deep occlusal bulk-fill resin composite restorations: A comparison of semi-split delayed gap closure and conventional bulk filling techniques using microcomputed tomography.
abstract: Polymerization shrinkage in bulk-fill resin composite restorations can lead to interfacial gap formation in deep occlusal cavities, compromising restoration integrity and longevity. Whether the semi-split delayed gap closure method reduces gap formation over conventional bulk filling is unclear. The purpose of this in vitro study was to compare the effect of the semi-split delayed gap closure and the conventional bulk filling technique on interfacial gap formation in deep occlusal bulk-fill resin composite restorations using microcomputed tomography (µCT). Tetric N-Etch etching gel, Tetric N-Bond Universal adhesive, and Tetric N-Ceram Bulk Fill resin composite (Ivoclar AG) were used for all adhesive and restorative procedures. Standardized Class I, square-shaped cavities (3×3 mm and 4 mm deep) were prepared in 24 extracted human molars. Specimens were allocated into 2 groups according to the restorative technique used (n=12 per group): an experimental group and a control group. In the experimental group, cavities were restored using the semi-split delayed gap closure technique. A 4-mm bulk of bulk-fill resin composite was placed in each cavity, and a diagonal gap (1.5 mm wide×2.0 mm deep) was created in the unpolymerized resin composite bulk, followed by initial light polymerization. The gap was left unfilled for 5 minutes and then filled with resin composite before final polymerization. In the control group, cavities were restored using the conventional bulk filling techniqu

Whether the semi-split delayed gap closure method reduces gap formation over conventional bulk filling is unclear.

Fermented Foods Target Multiple Hallmarks of Aging to Promote Healthy Longevity.
abstract: Aging is associated with progressive physiological decline driven by chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, immune dysfunction, and gut microbial dysbiosis, and fermented foods contain probiotics and bioactive metabolites that may beneficially influence these processes. This narrative review summarizes evidence on fermented foods and mechanisms associated with healthy aging, particularly gut microbiota composition, immune function, oxidative stress, and inflammation, while explicitly distinguishing findings from cell-based (in vitro) systems, animal (in vivo) models, and human participants. Each finding is labeled by its evidence tier so the strength and translational relevance of the data can be judged transparently. In vitro studies using cultured cells, including senescent fibroblasts, immune cells, and cancer cell lines, show that fermentation-derived metabolites can activate antioxidant, autophagic, and anti-inflammatory signaling pathways, and studies in rodent models, principally aged mice, show that fermented foods and their metabolites can improve mitochondrial function, reduce inflammatory markers, and reshape the gut microbiota. title: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular longevity-what is established, what is hypothesis?
abstract: Cardiovascular aging is the rate-limiting process for human life expectancy and healthspan. Nutrition and metabolism are the most widely available geroprotective targets, yet the underlying evidence is markedly uneven. To define which nutritional and metabolic interventions are established for cardiovascular longevity, or better healthy aging, and which remain hypothetical. Narrative review of randomized trials, cohort studies, and mechanistic work on dietary patterns, energy balance, meal timing, food quality, supplements, and biomarkers of biological aging. Whole dietary patterns (Mediterranean, "Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension" [DASH], sodium reduction) reduce hard cardiovascular endpoints, and the causal roles of apolipoprotein B (apoB)-containing lipoproteins, blood pressure, and adiposity are firmly established. Pharmacologically induced weight loss via glucagon-like peptide‑1 (GLP-1)-based drugs reduces cardiovascular events to a degree not achieved by lifestyle programs, shifting clinical nutrition toward preservation of lean mass and micronutrient adequacy. By contrast, isolated nutrients and supplements, a specific geroprotective effect of intermittent fasting, and the clinical utility of epigenetic aging clocks remain unproven. Randomized caloric restriction slows the epigenetic pace of aging only modestly and has so far not demonstrated mortality benefit in humans. summary_short: Cardiovascular aging is the rate-limiting process for human life expectancy and healthspan. Nutrition and metabolism are the most widely available geroprotective targets, yet the underlying evidence is markedly uneven.

title: Goals, motives, and methods of partner influence on cigarette smoking within sexual and/or gender minoritized dual-smoking couples: A qualitative study.
abstract: Introduction Couples wherein both members smoke cigarettes are highly prevalent and unlikely to achieve abstinence. It is known that romantic partners influence one another's smoking behaviors, but little is known about how, why, and to what end. Moreover, few studies have focused on relationships and smoking among marginalized groups despite disproportionate representation of marginalized identities among people who smoke. This qualitative study aimed to characterize attempts to influence partner smoking behaviors within sexual and/or gender minoritized (SGM) dual-smoking couples (DSCs). Methods SGM individuals in a DSC (N=28) were recruited nationally in the United States in 2025. Participants completed a 60-minute semi-structured in-depth interview regarding their relationship's dynamics around smoking and cessation. Analysis followed a team-based, deductive-inductive thematic approach to characterize partners' goals, motives, and methods of attempts to influence smoking and cessation behavior. Results Goals of influencing partner smoking ranged from reducing or stopping to maintaining or increasing smoking. Motives related to health (e.g., partner longevity), finances (e.g., cost of cigarettes), and/or relationship functioning (e.g., avoiding conflict). Methods of influence were verbal (e.g., self-distancing), behavioral (e.g., employing joint strategies), and strategic inaction (e.g., normalizing non-discussion of cessation). Conclusions This SGM-DSC study identified sev
summary_short: Introduction Couples wherein both members smoke cigarettes are highly prevalent and unlikely to achieve abstinence. It is known that romantic partners influence one another's smoking behaviors, but little is known about how, why, and to what end.

title: LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.
abstract: Different species can have various maximum lifespans, some with exceptional longevity, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Despite rapid advances in single-cell transcriptomics, resources that systematically connect single-cell gene expression profiles to species lifespan are limited. We hereby present the Longevity & Aging Cell Atlas (LACA), a database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets across 134 species with their maximum lifespans. LACA includes over 148 million cells with 190 annotated cell types from single-cell datasets. LACA also has a cross-species analytical toolbox of longevity gene comparison, gene-lifespan correlation, and cell-lifespan correlation. These tools allow researchers to better interpret both evolutionarily conserved longevity mechanisms and the evolution of species-specific adaptations in longevity mechanisms without extensive computational expertise. LACA also provides a centenarian single-cell atlas and a human immune aging multi-omics atlas, demonstrating the analytical capability of the resource, as well as 11 different modules for longevity-related analysis, an integrated knowledge graph including curated longevity knowledge bases, and a retrieval-augmented research agent to further facilitate functional interpretation. The database is freely available at https://www.longevityaging.net/ or http://8.142.154.29/LACA/.

title: Incremental associations of pharmacological components in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction: a systematic review and component network meta-analysis.
abstract: We conducted a component network meta-analysis (CNMA) of phase 3/4 randomized trials to evaluate incremental effects of pharmacological therapies in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF; LVEF > 40%). MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane were searched through 1 August 2025 (updated 30 March 2026). We performed an additive CNMA evaluating cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) and assessed certainty of evidence. Twenty-four trials and five secondary reports were included. The primary network was sparse (10 trials, 12 regimens), constraining interaction detection and component stability. Incretin-based interventions (pooling semaglutide and tirzepatide, iHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.53-0.91), SGLT-2 inhibitors (0.80, 0.74-0.88), ARNis (0.82, 0.68-0.99), and MRAs (0.89, 0.81-0.98) showed significant component associations, driven principally by fewer HFHs. No drug class significantly reduced mortality. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs remained significant across sensitivity analyses except LVEF ≥ 50%, with SGLT-2 inhibitors most precise. ARNi benefits lost significance under stricter background therapy thresholds (>60%) and contemporary trial restrictions. Evidence for incretins was low-certainty and sensitive to trial selection. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs provide the most robust incremental benefit, while evidence for other drug classes remains context-dependent. These findings should guide research priorities rather than define combi
summary_short: We conducted a component network meta-analysis (CNMA) of phase 3/4 randomized trials to evaluate incremental effects of pharmacological therapies in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF; LVEF > 40%). No drug class significantly reduced mortality.

title: Skeletal and metabolic effects of anti-sclerostin antibody therapy after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass in an obese ovariectomized mice.
abstract: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) provides long-term metabolic benefits but accelerates bone loss, particularly in postmenopausal individuals. Circulating sclerostin levels have been reported to increase after RYGB in postmenopausal women, suggesting that sclerostin inhibition may mitigate post-surgical skeletal deterioration. To determine whether anti-sclerostin antibody (Scl-Ab) therapy improves skeletal and metabolic outcomes following RYGB in an obese, ovariectomized (OVX) murine model. Female C57BL/6 J mice were fed a high-fat diet to induce obesity, underwent OVX, and were assigned to RYGB or weight-matched sham surgery. Mice received Scl-Ab or saline for eight weeks. Skeletal outcomes were assessed by three-point bending, micro-computed tomography, histology, and histomorphometry. Metabolic outcomes included glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, multiplex hormone profiling, and evaluation of the regulation of sclerostin by glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) in primary periosteal cells. In RYGB mice, Scl-Ab improved femoral biomechanical properties and trabecular bone architecture, increasing trabecular bone area and thickness. It also enhanced glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and circulating GLP-1, gastric inhibitory peptide, and secretin levels. In contrast, Scl-Ab further increased RYGB-associated cortical porosity, highlighting divergent effects on trabecular and cortical bone. title: Laundered Survival: When Target Trial Emulation Doesn't Emulate-Implications for GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Cancer Outcomes.
abstract: Target trial emulation (TTE) is increasingly invoked in observational studies to address time-related biases. Recent observational studies reporting large protective associations between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and cancer outcomes have cited TTE as a methodological strength. TTE validity, however, depends on explicit alignment of eligibility, treatment assignment, and time zero when outcome start to be counted (EAT0). We conducted a conceptual and quantitative evaluation of two recent observational studies that defined GLP-1 RA exposure using post-baseline information (≥2 prescriptions) while initiating follow-up at the first prescription. We reproduced these designs using Monte Carlo simulation (500 replications; n = 5,000 per replication) under a null treatment effect (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.0), varying the interval between first and second prescriptions. Analyses enforcing EAT0 alignment were used as comparators. By deferring treatment assignment while accruing person-time from an earlier index date, these designs violate a core requirement of TTE. This structure induces immortal time bias through both exposure misclassification and survivor selection. Simulated analyses reproducing these features generated HRs ranging from 0.72 to 0.39 in longer follow-up settings and from 0.85 to 0.60 in shorter follow-up settings, closely approximating published estimates. In contrast, analyses aligning time zero with treatment initiation eliminated the bias
summary_short: Target trial emulation (TTE) is increasingly invoked in observational studies to address time-related biases. Recent observational studies reporting large protective associations between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and cancer outcomes have cited TTE as a methodological strength.

title: Cancer risk with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
abstract: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). title: Where patients obtain GLP-1 receptor agonists: direct-to-consumer channels, compounded product use, and reason-specific nonadherence in a national survey.
abstract: To examine acquisition channels for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and associations with compounded use, prescription status, and nonadherence. This cross-sectional analysis used the National Center for Health Statistics Rapid Surveys System Round 7 (July-August 2025; N = 8118). Among 976 past-year users, channels were classified as clinician/pharmacy without direct-to-consumer (DTC) acquisition, any DTC telehealth/medical spa, or other. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs). GLP-1 RA use was reported by 9.8% of adults, approximately 25.9 million. Of users, 18.3% used a DTC or medical spa channel and 9.2% reported no clinician prescription. Among users reporting known compounded status, compounded use was 73.0% (95% CI, 62.7%-81.2%) for DTC versus 12.9% (8.8%-18.4%) for conventional acquisition (aOR, 14.56; 95% CI, 7.99-26.54). Overall, 22.6% reported compounded use and 8.6% did not know. DTC acquisition was associated with cost-attributed nonadherence (aOR, 4.94; 95% CI, 2.77-8.81); the supply-attributed association was not statistically significant (aOR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.56-2.38; contrast P < 0.001). Associations were also observed for side-effect-attributed reduction/discontinuation (aOR, 2.12; 95% CI, 1.05-4.27) and complete discontinuation (aOR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.01-3.32). Counseling associations were imprecise. Insurance nonpayment was associated with DTC acquisition (aOR, 8.01; 95% CI, 4.70-13.67). DTC acquisition

Insurance nonpayment was associated with DTC acquisition (aOR, 8.01; 95% CI, 4.70-13.67).

Advanced Medical Therapeutic Approaches to Treat Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCSs) encompass obstructive and non-obstructive coronary artery disease, including epicardial atherosclerosis, coronary microvascular dysfunction, and coronary vasospasm, which may lead to angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, heart attack, and sudden death. Understanding the pathophysiology of CCS has led to targeted therapeutic approaches aimed at managing dyslipidemia, inflammation, and thrombus formation to reduce cardiovascular burden and mortality risk. This review aimed to explore advanced and emerging therapeutic strategies for the treatment of CCS, including advanced lipid-lowering therapies, Lp(a)-lowering RNA agents, novel anti-inflammatory agents, including interleukin-6 (IL-6)-targeted therapy, Factor XIa-targeted antithrombotic therapy, cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors (CETP), angiopoietin-like protein 3 (ANGPTL3) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), nanoparticle-based targeted therapies, and microbiome-modifying therapies. title: Real-World Weight Changes of Prescribed Semaglutide Medications and Application of a Novel Cognitive-Behavioral Protocol: A Nonrandomized 12-Month Retrospective Assessment of Women With Obesity.
abstract: Introduction A plethora of data are available on the unsatisfactory outcomes of obesity treatments focused on controlling eating and increasing exercise/physical activity. As a result, there has been an increase in the prescription of semaglutide medications for weight loss. Although 12-month weight reductions associated with such pharmacologic treatments are reported to range from 12% to 18% within controlled settings, lesser reductions are indicated under "real-word" conditions, where treatment compliance is, overall, less favorable. Prior research has also indicated that an evolving cognitive-behavioral obesity treatment that focuses on exercise-related psychological changes carrying over to changes in eating behaviors within real-world settings might improve the weight-loss effects associated with previous behavioral means. Objective The aims of this work were to position future research and generate hypotheses relating to such treatment modalities, especially under randomized conditions. Methods Real-world weight-change data from women with obesity associated with treatments using semaglutide (n = 314) or theory-based cognitive-behavioral processes focused on enhancing self-regulation, initially through increased exercise (n = 95), were measured from baseline to month 12. title: Natural Products Targeting Metabolic Disorders in Diabetic Kidney Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes. Although the emergence of new therapies such as SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, aldosterone receptor antagonists, and endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs) has expanded the therapeutic options for DKD, these therapies remain insufficient to meet the urgent clinical needs of contemporary society. Recent studies indicate that the pathogenesis of DKD involves multiple signaling pathways and drug targets. DKD is closely linked to the dysregulation of glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism. Compared to synthetic drugs, natural products offer advantages such as broader biological activities, favorable drug-like potential, multi-target mechanisms of action, enhanced safety and tolerability profiles, as well as abundant and renewable sources. Over the past two decades, natural products have demonstrated considerable potential in preclinical DKD studies (triptolide, quercetin, berberine, baicalin, resveratrol, proanthocyanidin B2), and various natural compounds are now considered integral components of comprehensive DKD management strategies, despite their disadvantages of poor solubility and low bioavailability. This review focuses on the cellular and molecular mechanisms through which natural products alleviate DKD by targeting metabolic disorders, summarizes the contributions of nanodelivery systems in improving the bioavailability of natural products, and presents related challenges in
summary_short: Recent studies indicate that the pathogenesis of DKD involves multiple signaling pathways and drug targets.

title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitors in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
abstract: Background Heart transplant (HT) recipients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face elevated risks of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV), rejection, and cardiovascular events. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) confer cardiorenal protection in general T2DM patients, but data specific to HT recipients are scarce. Methods We conducted a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adult HT recipients with T2DM who initiated a GLP-1 RA or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor after transplantation between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2025, were matched 1:1 on 36 covariates. The primary outcome was a 3-year graft-specific composite of CAV (T86.290), HT rejection (T86.21), or HT failure (T86.22). All-cause mortality and myocardial infarction (I21) or ischemic stroke (I63) were analyzed separately. Results After matching, 712 patients per group were analyzed. At 3 y, the graft-specific composite occurred in 12.1% of GLP-1 RA recipients versus 29.2% of DPP-4 inhibitor recipients (risk ratio [RR] 0.416; 95% confidence interval, 0.299-0.579; P Conclusions In this multicenter electronic health record-based cohort, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower graft-specific outcomes and all-cause mortality than DPP-4 inhibitor use. CAV did not differ significantly. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

title: A novel role of NOX2 in enhancing HBV replication through ROS‑mediated autophagy activation.
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious global public health issue. Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the underlying mechanisms by which NOX2 affects HBV infection remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the potential role of NOX2 in HBV replication was investigated in cell models. First, it was demonstrated that NOX2 is highly expressed in transiently and stably HBV‑infected cells. Second, by employing inhibitor, RNA interference technique and plasmid overexpression, it was revealed that NOX2 plays an essential role in promoting HBV replication. Furthermore, the underlying mechanism of how NOX2 affects HBV replication was illustrated. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication. These results suggested a previously unrecognized role of NOX2 in HBV replication. Taken together, NOX2 may serve as a novel target for developing treatment strategies against HBV‑related disorders.
summary_short: Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication.

Dissipation of lysosome pH impairs formation and collapses existing LPS-induced lysosome tubules in macrophages.
abstract: While lysosomes are typically globular in morphology, lipopolysaccharide-activated macrophages reorganize lysosomes into an expanded tubular network. Here, we sought to determine if the V-ATPase and the lysosomal pH contribute to LPS-mediated lysosome tubulation in macrophages. We found that inhibition of the V-ATPase prevented lysosome tubulation and collapsed preformed tubules. However, the V-ATPase also controls mTORC1 activity, which itself is needed for tubulation. To distinguish between lysosomal pH and mTORC1, we turned to NH 4 Cl, which alkalinized lysosomal pH but did not interfere with mTORC1; yet NH 4 Cl blocked tubulation, showing that an acidic lysosomal pH is needed for lysosome remodelling. Moreover, clamping the pH to either acidic or alkaline pH caused tubules to collapse, indicating that the pH gradient promotes tubulation, rather than a specific pH. These effects were not due to altered microtubule organization or impaired lysosome motility, suggesting that motors remained associated with lysosomes. On the other hand, while LPS did not alter the average pH of spherical or tubular lysosomes, growing tubules displayed a more acidic peripheral end relative to the pericentral end. Based on this observation, we propose that a localized pH gradient along the tubule may enable tubulation by modulating factors that catalyse tubule growth.
summary_short: We found that inhibition of the V-ATPase prevented lysosome tubulation and collapsed preformed tubules. These effects were not due to altered microtubule organization or impaired lysosome motility, suggesting that motors remained associated with lysosomes.

title: ATP and α-ketoglutarate link nitrogen availability to TORC1-Npr1 signaling in yeast.
abstract: The TORC1 (Target of Rapamycin Complex 1) kinase complex coordinates eukaryotic cell growth and metabolism in response to nutrient availability. In yeast, one of the proteins under TORC1 control is the Npr1 kinase mediating nitrogen control of several plasma membrane transporters, yet the metabolic signals governing this pathway remain poorly understood. Here, we first investigated the previously described and unexpected activation of TORC1-Npr1 signaling upon acute glucose starvation. We show that this response occurs only under specific nitrogen conditions, notably in cells grown on proline or glutamine, and depends on increased ATP production driven by stimulated respiration. In proline-grown cells, this respiration is fueled by catabolism of α-ketoglutarate, while high α-ketoglutarate levels negatively affect TORC1-Npr1 activation. We next analyzed TORC1-Npr1 activation following NH 4 + addition to proline-grown cells. Our results confirm that glutamine accumulation is not required for this activation and instead show that NH 4 + assimilation is associated with a decrease in α-ketoglutarate levels and a sustained increase in ATP production, concomitant with TORC1-Npr1 activation. In cells lacking the NH 4 + -assimilating glutamate dehydrogenases, both increased ATP production and TORC1-Npr1 activation are impaired. Together, these findings identify ATP and α-ketoglutarate as important metabolic determinants of TORC1-Npr1 signaling in response to nitrogen availability.

title: AKT as a central node integrating multidrug resistance mechanisms in ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality. Although HGSOC responds to platinum-taxane therapy, 70-85% relapse, with acquired resistance playing a major role. The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT)/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, centered on AKT, contributes to this resistance. Current literature examines AKT's downstream consequences in isolation, overlooking their collective contribution to tumor evolution; this review addresses that gap by separating upstream AKT activation from downstream resistance outputs. Intrinsic genomic alterations (PIK3CA mutation, phosphatase and tensin homolog [PTEN] loss) and extrinsic tumor microenvironment (TME) cues converge on AKT, which drives four emerging resistance mechanisms (metabolic reprogramming and ferroptosis evasion, epigenetic modulation of homologous recombination inhibitor sensitivity, cancer stem cell plasticity, and immune evasion, discussed with therapeutic targeting), integrated with classical mechanisms into a unified chemoresistance framework. AKT promotes chemoresistance by coordinating ATP-binding cassette transporter-mediated drug efflux, RAD51/BRCA-dependent DNA repair, and an elevated apoptotic threshold via Bcl-2-associated agonist of cell death and survivin modulation. Spatial organization and interconnections are highlighted, including amplified AKT activation at the tumor-stromal interface throu
summary_short: Ovarian cancer, particularly high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality. Although HGSOC responds to platinum-taxane therapy, 70-85% relapse, with acquired resistance playing a major role.

title: Dietary alanyl-glutamine modulates glutamine metabolism, mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling and metabolic homeostasis in juvenile mud crab (Scylla paramamosain).
abstract: The mechanisms by which alanyl-glutamine (Ala-Gln) may affect growth and intestinal function in juvenile mud crab remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study evaluated growth, nutrient metabolism, and intestinal health in juvenile mud crab (Scylla paramamosain). A total of 108 crabs (5.91 ± 0.22 g) received three isonitrogenous and isolipidic diets containing 0%, 1% or 2% supplemental Ala-Gln for 9 weeks. Both supplementation levels improved growth, feed utilization and muscle protein content, without significant differences between them. Supplementation increased hepatopancreatic glutamine and glutamate concentrations and glutaminase and glutamate dehydrogenase activities. These responses were accompanied by enhanced mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling, reduced hepatopancreatic lipid accumulation, and increased glycogen and pyruvate contents. Intestinal morphology improved at 2%, alongside changes in apoptosis-related and barrier-associated gene and protein expression. Overall, Ala-Gln supplementation improved growth and feed utilization in association with changes in glutamine metabolism, mTOR-related signaling and intestinal characteristics. Increasing supplementation from 1% to 2% did not consistently provide additional benefits, and an optimal supplementation level remains undetermined. The absence of an equimolar free alanine-glutamine control precludes attribution of the observed benefits specifically to the dipeptide form.
summary_short: Intestinal morphology improved at 2%, alongside changes in apoptosis-related and barrier-associated gene and protein expression. Overall, Ala-Gln supplementation improved growth and feed utilization in association with changes in glutamine metabolism, mTOR-related signaling and intestinal characteristics.

title: Age-Stratified Sirolimus Trough Concentrations in Pediatric Vascular Malformations: A Real-World Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background Sirolimus is increasingly being used off-label to treat pediatric vascular malformations. In this study, the age-stratified drug exposure, pharmacokinetic variability, and long-term treatment characteristics of sirolimus were evaluated in a real-world pediatric population. Methods In this study, 144 patients (younger than 19 years) with vascular malformations who were treated with sirolimus at a single center (July 2018 and March 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. A total of 2054 therapeutic drug monitoring measurements were obtained. The patients were stratified into 6 age groups (1 month and younger to 12-18 years). The outcomes included trough concentration, interindividual variability (coefficient of variation), target range attainment, treatment duration, and MRI-based response. Results The median follow-up was 18.3 months (range, 0.3-74.1 months). Neonates (1 month and younger) showed the highest interindividual variability (coefficient of variation = 61.6%), with lower variability observed in adolescents (40.0%, P 15 ng/mL) were most frequent in neonates (6.6%). Prolonged therapy (≥24 months) was observed in 31.9% of patients, with a median duration of 35.1 months. Among the 44 patients who underwent follow-up MRI, 84.1% showed disease improvement or stability. Conclusions Sustained long-term treatment continuity suggests that sirolimus was generally tolerated across pediatric age groups, although direct toxicity data were not systematically captured in th

title: Target of rapamycin and regulation of membrane transporters: integrating nutrient sensing, stress adaptation and lifespan across eukaryotes.
abstract: Nutrient availability is typically treated as an input to the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway, the conserved controller of growth, metabolism and ageing. Yet, membrane transporters are not merely suppliers of the amino acids and other nutrients that activate TOR, they are integral components of the signalling network itself, and TOR in turn governs their activity, abundance, trafficking and degradation. This bidirectional coupling - including transporters that double as receptors, or 'transceptors' - is mechanistically defined in budding yeast, where the TORC1 complex acts through the Npr1-arrestin axis and vacuolar Gtr/EGO amino acid sensing, conserved in fission yeast, where TOR links nitrogen transport and vacuolar function to growth, stress and lifespan; and elaborated in metazoans across intestinal and fat-body uptake, endocrine relays and lysosomal gatekeepers such as SLC38A9, NPC1 and TRPML1. We propose that TOR-transporter coupling offers a conserved and mechanistically compelling, but still, largely untested, route linking nutrient transport to stress resistance and lifespan across eukaryotes and we advance it as a framework to guide future causal work rather than a settled conclusion.

title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in T‑cell exhaustion: Its contribution to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy (Review).
abstract: Mitochondria play a pivotal role in the regulation of T‑cell function, particularly in the context of T‑cell exhaustion within the tumor microenvironment. T‑cell exhaustion, characterized by impaired effector functions and the sustained expression of inhibitory receptors, poses a significant barrier to effective antitumor immunity and limits the success of immunotherapies. Emerging evidence indicates that mitochondrial dysfunction is a contributor to the metabolic and functional decline of tumor‑infiltrating lymphocytes. The present review critically synthesizes the available mechanistic and translational literature on mitochondrial dysfunction in T‑cell exhaustion, with particular attention paid to mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and the threshold‑dependent duality of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species. The evidence is organized not by pathway alone, but by intervention class and level of evidence, so that the strategies with demonstrated clinical traction can be distinguished from those that remain at the proof‑of‑concept stage. Of note, four intervention classes are discussed: Metabolic reprogramming, enhancement of mitochondrial biogenesis, redox‑directed modulation and intercellular mitochondrial transfer, together with mitochondria‑directed pharmacological and nanoscale delivery platforms. Clinical translation is assessed against trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, of which the most advanced evaluate metformin in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
summary_short: Emerging evidence indicates that mitochondrial dysfunction is a contributor to the metabolic and functional decline of tumor‑infiltrating lymphocytes.

title: Metformin mitigates trophoblast GLUT1 inhibition through HIF-1α/Fibronectin/AMPK pathway in preeclampsia.
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a complex gestational hypertensive disorder associated with dysregulated placental energy metabolism, and fibronectin (FN) plays a critical role in its development. Although metformin has shown potential in reducing the risk of PE, its effects on FN and trophoblast glucose transport regulation remain unclear. In this study, experiments were conducted using FN-pretreated and FN-knockdown HTR-8/SVneo cells, clinical placental specimens, and a preeclampsia mouse model. Aberrant FN and GLUT1 expression was observed in human preeclamptic placentas. Under hypoxic conditions, FN and GLUT1 were upregulated in two trophoblastic cell lines (HTR-8/SVneo and JAR) and in primary placental cells. However, exogenous FN suppressed hypoxia-associated GLUT1 upregulation, reduced extracellular L-lactate levels, and impaired trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. These effects were associated with activation of AMPK signaling. Metformin reduced HIF-1α, FN, and phosphorylated AMPK levels in FN-treated trophoblasts under hypoxia, while increasing GLUT1 expression and extracellular L-lactate levels and restoring trophoblast invasion and ciliogenesis. Notably, metformin increased AMPK phosphorylation in FN-silenced cells, suggesting that its effects on AMPK signaling depend, at least partly, on FN status. title: GnRH-a Plus Letrozole vs Ethinylestradiol/Cyproterone Acetate Plus Metformin in Progestin-Insensitive Endometrial Atypical Hyperplasia: A Multicenter Phase II RCT.
abstract: Effective second-line fertility-preserving treatment for progestin-insensitive endometrial atypical hyperplasia (EAH) has not been established. We compare the efficacy and safety of gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist (GnRH-a) plus letrozole with ethinylestradiol/cyproterone acetate (Diane-35) plus metformin in this population. In this multicenter, open-label, randomized phase II trial, patients aged 18-45 years with progestin-insensitive EAH seeking fertility preservation were assigned 1:1 to GnRH-a plus letrozole or Diane-35 plus metformin. Treatment response was assessed by scheduled hysteroscopy with pathological evaluation. The primary endpoint was the complete response (CR) rate within 28 weeks after second-line treatment initiation. Secondary endpoints reported in this analysis included time to CR, adverse events and compliance. From July 2022 to July 2025, 41 patients were randomized and analyzed by intention-to-treat analysis. CR within 28 weeks was achieved in 19 of 20 patients (95.0%) in the GnRH-a plus letrozole group and 14 of 21 patients (66.7%) in the Diane-35 plus metformin group, corresponding to a risk difference of 28.3 percentage points (95% CI, 3.7-50.0; two-sided Fisher's exact P=0.045). title: Long-term metformin therapy and risk of anemia in type 2 diabetes.
abstract: Metformin is the cornerstone therapy for type 2 diabetes (T2D) and is prescribed long term to large patient populations, making its potential hematological effects clinically relevant. Particular attention has focused on metformin-associated vitamin B12 deficiency and its possible contribution to anemia. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that metformin reduces serum vitamin B12 concentrations and increases the risk of biochemical deficiency, particularly with higher doses and prolonged treatment. However, its overall effects on hemoglobin levels and anemia risk remain modest and variable across clinical populations. Importantly, anemia in patients with T2D is multifactorial and may result from chronic kidney disease, iron deficiency, systemic inflammation, blood loss, or other nutritional deficiencies, complicating the identification of metformin's independent contribution. Although vitamin B12 depletion represents a plausible mechanism linking metformin exposure to hematological abnormalities, additional metabolic and clinical factors may influence erythropoiesis and hemoglobin homeostasis. Furthermore, longer treatment duration and greater cumulative exposure may increase the likelihood of vitamin B12 deficiency, highlighting the importance of appropriate clinical surveillance. title: Taurine Protects Against Paclitaxel-Induced Testicular Injury in Adult Rats by Mitigating Oxidative Stress and Apoptotic Cell Death.
abstract: To evaluate the protective effects of taurine against paclitaxel-induced testicular, hormonal, metabolic, and molecular alterations in male rats. Adult male rats were randomly allocated into four groups (n = 8 per group): control, taurine alone (150mg/kg/day), paclitaxel alone (2mg/kg every other day), and paclitaxel plus taurine. title: Mitochondrial–ER contact sites in skeletal muscle: a central hub in anabolic resistance and sarcopenia
abstract: Mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites (MERCs) are critical structural hubs that integrate cellular signaling, bioenergetics and proteostasis. In skeletal muscle, a tissue exceptionally vulnerable to age-related decline, MERCs physically and functionally link mitochondria with the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR), with mitochondria to govern excitation–contraction coupling, coordinating calcium (Ca 2+ ) homeostasis and metabolic homeostasis. While Sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss) and anabolic resistance—the blunted hypertrophic response to nutrition or contractile stimuli, have traditionally been attributed to factors such as mitochondrial dysfunction, hormonal shifts, and chronic low-grade inflammation, growing evidence positions MERCs as a spatial nexus where these pathogenic processes converge. This review examines fundamental biology of muscle MERCs, detailing their specialized molecular architecture, tethering complexes, and physiological roles in Ca 2+ dynamics, bioenergetics, and proteostasis. We then evaluate how aging perturbs MERC ultrastructure characterized by the loss of structural tethers and progressive widening of SR-mitochondrial gaps and discuss how these changes are not merely correlative but are potentially mechanistically linked to impaired anabolic signaling. title: Estimated pulse wave velocity acceleration is an algebraic function of its own inputs: incremental prognostic value of blood-based biological age beyond chronological age and blood pressure in older US and Chinese adults
abstract: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is widely reported as a measure of vascular age, yet it is computed from chronological age and mean blood pressure (MBP); whether its age-residualized component, ePWV acceleration, carries information beyond those inputs has never been tested. Among 3972 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) participants aged 60 or older (1034 deaths, 330 cardiovascular) we asked whether ePWV acceleration is a quantity distinct from its own inputs, and compared its prognostic value with blood-based biological age, based on PhenoAge and the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM), for all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, validating the comparison in two Chinese cohorts (CHARLS, n = 7892; CLHLS, n = 560). Within each risk branch of the estimating equation, ePWV acceleration was reproduced exactly from its own inputs ( R 2 approximately 1; residual standard deviation below 1 × 10 ⁻11 m/s) and correlated 0.990 with MBP, whereas the blood-based accelerations were uncorrelated with MBP. PhenoAge acceleration (hazard ratio per standard deviation 1.82, 95% confidence interval 1.68 to 1.97) and KDM acceleration (1.64, 1.53 to 1.76) predicted mortality, were well calibrated, retained incremental discrimination once spline age and MBP were modeled (change in Harrell C + 0.036 and + 0.032), and did so under machine-learning survival models and in both Chinese cohorts. ePWV acceleration added none (− 0.0001) and was not jointly estimable with MBP. title: Clonal hematopoiesis and the risk of major age-related eye diseases
abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), an age-related hematologic condition associated with systemic inflammation, has uncertain associations with major eye diseases. We aimed to investigate the association of CHIP, including its major genetic subtypes and clone sizes, with the risk of cataract, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy (DR). UK Biobank participants enrolled during 2006–2010 were followed by linked electronic health records until March 2022. Whole-exome sequencing identified CHIP as somatic driver mutations with variant allele frequency ≥ 2%. Multivariable Cox regression was applied to assess hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). The DR analysis was restricted to participants with diabetes. Of 436,469 participants (mean age, 56.4 years; 54.5% women), 14,110 (3.2%) had CHIP. During a median 14.4-year follow-up, 31,165 cataract, 12,393 glaucoma, 13,644 AMD, and 2,692 DR diagnoses occurred. CHIP was associated with cataract (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [1.03–1.14]), AMD (HR [95%CI]: 1.12 [1.04–1.21]), and DR (HR [95%CI]: 1.48 [1.25–1.74]), but the association with glaucoma overall did not reach statistical significance (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [0.99–1.17]). The glaucoma association was statistically significant among participants without hypertension (HR [95%CI]: 1.22 [1.06–1.40]; P for interaction = 0.012). title: Macadamia Nut Oil Alleviates Aβ-Induced Neurotoxicity and Extends Lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by Modulating the DAF-16/SKN-1 Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Macadamia nut oil (MNO) represents a well-recognized functional lipid rich in unsaturated fatty acids, but its neuroprotective properties remain poorly elucidated. This study sought to evaluate the neuroprotective potential of MNO and explore its underlying mechanisms in an in vivo Caenorhabditis elegans model. In this study, the in vitro antioxidant capacity of MNO was determined via chemical antioxidant assays. The results indicated that MNO possessed strong scavenging activities against ABTS, DPPH, and hydroxyl radicals. Further in vivo experiments were performed using C. elegans as the model organism. MNO treatment dose-dependently delayed Aβ-mediated paralysis and ameliorated chemotaxis ability. Moreover, MNO supplementation prolonged lifespan, reduced lipofuscin deposition, and improved nematode survival under heat, oxidative, and UV stress. Biochemical tests showed that MNO decreased ROS and MDA contents and increased the activities of SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px. RT-qPCR results revealed that MNO inhibited Aβ accumulation and daf-2 expression and upregulated longevity and stress-related genes including daf-16, skn-1, sod-3, gst-4, sir-2.1, and hsp-16.2. MNO promoted nuclear translocation of DAF-16 and SKN-1 and increased downstream sod-3 and gst-4 fluorescent reporter expression; mutant assays verified that both signaling pathways are indispensable for MNO-derived protection. title: Association between addiction consult exposure and provider adoption of buprenorphine initiation.
abstract: Background and objectives Addiction consult services (ACSs) increase inpatient treatment for opioid use disorder (OUD) and may support prescribing capacity among non-specialists. We evaluated whether cumulative provider-level ACS exposure was associated with independent buprenorphine initiation. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of providers caring for hospitalized adults with OUD at an academic medical center (2018-2026). Providers entered at their first qualifying inpatient or emergency department encounter. Cumulative ACS exposure at initiation or censoring was categorized as 0, 1-2, 3-5, or ≥6 ACS-involved encounters. The outcome was time to first observed buprenorphine initiation during an encounter without an ACS consult. Sensitivity analyses examined consult-exposed providers, study-entry era, and exclusion of ED providers. Results Among 3,410 providers, 582 (17.1%) independently initiated buprenorphine. Compared with providers with no ACS exposure, providers with ≥6 exposures had a higher average rate of independent initiation (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.74; 95% CI, 1.40-2.16), whereas estimates for 1-2 and 3-5 exposures were not significant. Among consult-exposed providers, ≥6 versus 1-2 exposures was associated with a higher initiation rate (aHR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.37-2.30). title: SPOP mutations impair CRL3<sup>SPOP</sup>-mediated survivin degradation to confer chemotherapy resistance in prostate cancer: implications for survivin-targeted therapy.
abstract: Dysregulated apoptosis is a critical factor contributing to the emergence of drug resistance in cancer chemotherapy. Survivin, a key member of the inhibitor of apoptosis protein (IAP) family, is frequently overexpressed in various cancers and plays a pivotal role in apoptosis regulation. In our study, we identified CRL3 SPOP as a canonical E3 ligase for survivin, mediating its ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Intriguingly, prostate cancer-associated SPOP mutants lose the ability to bind survivin, thereby impairing its degradation which leads to diminished apoptosis, enhanced cell survival, and increased chemotherapy resistance in prostate cancer cells harboring SPOP mutations. Importantly, we demonstrated that depletion of survivin in SPOP-mutated cells significantly enhances apoptosis and restores chemosensitivity. This study provides a direct mechanism for the reduced level of apoptosis in prostate cancer with SPOP mutations, and demonstrated that survivin might be a therapeutic target for SPOP-mutated patients and provided new strategies to overcome chemotherapy resistance.

title: Mismatch Negativity and General Cognitive Ability - A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Intelligence or general cognitive ability (GCA) is fundamental to human behavior and cognition. It impacts important life outcomes like educational success, and even health and longevity have been related to differences in GCA. Understanding the biological basis of such individual variations presents a crucial goal of neuroscience. The mismatch negativity (MMN) is an event-related brain potential that can be measured when-within a series of frequent standard stimuli, rare deviants are presented-and is suggested to reflect conscious (active) or unconscious (passive) detection processes of the brain. Importantly, variations in MMN amplitude and latency have been linked to differences in GCA. Yet findings vary considerably. This preregistered meta-analysis provides a comprehensive and structured overview of the current state of research. Following the study selection process in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, and the rating of study design quality with the Study Design and Implementation Assessment Device for Individual Difference Research (DIAD-ID), the association between GCA and MMN amplitude and latency was examined in 645 healthy adults across 12 included studies. The estimated across-sample associations between MMN and GCA were small, but significant (MMN amplitude-GCA: r = -0.09, MMN latency-GCA: r = -0.16; p < 0.01) and moderators were identified. Between-sample heterogeneity was moderate, with no evidence of publication bias. Our findings suggest that higher cogn

title: Closing the evidence gap: a life course and neurodiversity-informed participatory scoping review of healthy ageing randomised controlled trials in adults with developmental disabilities.
abstract: Adults aged 18 years and older with developmental disabilities experience disproportionate adverse health outcomes across the life course and shortened life expectancy. We conducted a participatory scoping review of randomised controlled trials of healthy ageing interventions for adults with developmental disabilities, informed by the WHO life course framework and neurodiversity principles. We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection on June 25, 2024, and April 10, 2025, and charted study characteristics and framework alignment. We included 79 trials with 8221 participants. Although 77 (97%) of 79 studies addressed at least one functional ability, only 25 (32%) targeted life course transitions, 28 (35%) targeted multiple ecosystem levels, 22 (28%) used participatory approaches, and 20 (25%) used strengths-based approaches. Life course and neurodiversity principles were incompletely integrated into intervention research, indicating opportunities to address developmental transitions, multiple ecosystem levels, social and community participation, and strengths across the life course.

title: Electrode material degradation and protection strategies in electrochemical wastewater treatment.
abstract: Electrochemical wastewater treatment technologies have emerged as promising green alternatives for the degradation of recalcitrant organic pollutants, offering compact design, minimal chemical input, and high process controllability. However, the long-term viability of these technologies is critically constrained by electrode degradation, which diminishes catalytic activity, increases energy consumption, and may generate secondary pollution through the leaching of toxic electrode constituents. From a green chemistry perspective, electrode longevity and material sustainability are paramount for ensuring that electrochemical treatment remains environmentally benign throughout its operational lifecycle. This review systematically examines the degradation mechanisms of electrode materials in three major electrochemical technologies-electrochemical oxidation, electrocoagulation, and electro-Fenton-and evaluates green protection strategies aimed at enhancing electrode durability. We discuss sustainable substrate selection, eco-friendly coating design, intermediate layer engineering, anti-fouling surface modification, self-healing coatings, operational optimization, and electrode regeneration and recycling. A comparative assessment of electrode materials is presented, highlighting their advantages, degradation modes, typical lifespans, and green credentials. The review concludes with a discussion of current challenges and future perspectives, emphasizing the integration of life-cycl

title: Multi-omics profiling reveals sex-dependent cardiac remodeling and SIRT4-associated metabolic patterns during late-life aging.
abstract: Extreme longevity is accompanied by cardiac molecular remodelling, yet the basis of sex-associated adaptation during late-life aging remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed cardiac proteomic and multi-compartment metabolomic profiling metabolomic profiling of heart tissue, serum, and urine from naturally long-lived male and female mice across late-life aging stages. Multi-omics analyses revealed pronounced sexual dimorphism during extreme cardiac aging. Proteomic and metabolic changes varied between sexes and across aging transitions, particularly in pathways related to mitochondrial metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid metabolism, and redox homeostasis. Trajectory analyses further demonstrated dynamic and non-linear aging patterns, with distinct temporal patterns observed between males and females across molecular compartments. Among the identified molecular features, SIRT4 emerged as a candidate showing a prominent age-associated change in the female cardiac proteome and associations with mitochondrial metabolic processes. In addition, SIRT4-centered metabolic networks in identified associations between SIRT4 abundance and metabolic features across cardiac and systemic compartments, with more associations observed in females than in males. title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Agonists or Tezepelumab for Obesity-Associated Asthma: A Cohort Study.
abstract: Rationale Obesity is associated with poor asthma outcomes. GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists induce weight loss and dampen airway inflammation independent of pathways currently targeted by biologics. Objective To compare differences in respiratory outcomes and weight loss between GLP-1-based medications and tezepelumab in asthma patients without diabetes. Methods A retrospective study was performed in a multi-institutional electronic health record database. Patients with specialist-treated, obesity-associated, moderate-to-severe asthma with at least one severe exacerbation in the prior year who initiated liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide, or tezepelumab between January 1, 2022 and December 31, 2025 were identified. Prevalent diabetes was excluded. Patients were followed for subsequent exacerbations, rescue inhaler prescriptions, respiratory-related healthcare encounters, and time to greater than 10% loss in body mass index. Overlap weighting accounted for imbalance in baseline asthma and obesity characteristics. Results 2779 patients were identified, of whom 133 initiated liraglutide, 1770 semaglutide, 472 tirzepatide, and 404 tezepelumab. In weighted estimates, patients starting tirzepatide experienced a lower hazard of severe exacerbation compared to tezepelumab (weighted hazard ratio [wHR] 0.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.24-0.70); those starting semaglutide had a similar hazard (wHR 0.99; 95% CI 0.70-1.39). title: Managing post-bariatric weight recurrence with new obesity management medications.
abstract: Recurrent weight gain (RWG) following metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) represents a major challenge in the long-term management of obesity and is distinct from insufficient weight loss and suboptimal clinical response, which reflect a primary inadequate response. RWG is defined as regain of ≥25% of the maximum weight lost, assessed ≥24 months after surgery. It affects approximately 35% of patients within 5 years of sleeve gastrectomy and approximately 15% within 5 years after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. With longer follow-up, the number of affected patients rises to about one-third. RWG is multifactorial: genetic predisposition, preoperative metabolic phenotype, inadequate or failed surgical anatomy, and neurohormonal and adipose tissue adaptations interact over time to cause it, and no single variable accounts for it. Randomized evidence indicates that the operation itself is a determinant of long-term response: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass elicits greater postprandial GLP1 secretion, more durable weight loss and higher rates of type 2 diabetes mellitus remission than sleeve gastrectomy, so procedure selection warrants as much attention as postoperative management. Treatment should therefore be specific to phenotype and procedure, escalating from lifestyle optimization to obesity management medications, endoscopic revision and revisional surgery, if needed. title: Impacts of medications for obesity on global health and the environment.
abstract: A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. We apply a global food system model to project the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1) uptake to 2050 among people with obesity under two scenarios: reduced calorie intake while maintaining dietary composition, and reduced calorie intake combined with shifts towards the EAT-Lancet diet. Compared with the Reference scenario, GLP-1-mediated calorie reduction alone results in up to 6.6 million avoided deaths globally in 2050 and 32 Mha more natural land area, reflecting reductions in cropland, pasture and managed forest. Combining GLP-1 use with EAT-Lancet dietary shifts increases these estimates to 7.7 million avoided deaths and 46 Mha more natural land. Lower food prices increase food consumption among untreated populations, including unhealthy foods, partially offsetting these gains.
summary_short: We apply a global food system model to project the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1) uptake to 2050 among people with obesity under two scenarios: reduced calorie intake while maintaining dietary composition, and reduced calorie intake combined with shifts towards the EAT-Lancet diet.

title: Testosterone Added to Incretin Therapy in Men With Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review of Body Composition Evidence and Gaps.
abstract: Aims To characterize body-composition evidence and muscle and safety gaps for testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) added to incretin treatment in men with overweight or obesity and hypogonadism. Materials and methods PROSPERO CRD420261489220. Seven databases and two registries were searched through 4 September 2026; citations were checked on 10 September. Eligible studies compared concurrent TRT with a comparable incretin regimen without TRT or examined baseline androgen status longitudinally. The original eight reports underwent independent assessment. Following joint initial screening, 300 randomly sampled units were independently rescreened. ROBINS-I, RoB 2 and GRADE informed synthesis by design and outcome. Results Two reports provided non-equivalent body-composition outcomes with very low certainty. Neither established incremental TRT benefit. In a nonrandomized pilot (five men per group), the final DXA lean-mass difference was +2.70 kg (exploratory, unadjusted 95% CI -1.75 to +7.15); the descriptive difference in changes was +2.1 kg, with change-score dispersion unavailable. A randomized conference report (266 men across five arms; comparison-arm sizes unavailable) attributed 26% versus 38% of weight loss to fat-free mass with versus without TRT. These observations do not corroborate a common biological effect. No usable TRT-specific strength, function or safety comparisons or eligible baseline-androgen analyses were identified. title: Effects of a Prebiotic Functional Soda on Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Adults Receiving GLP-1-Based Therapy for Weight Management: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.

title: Associations of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Usage With Clinical Outcomes of Limb Osteomyelitis in Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: Purpose Patients with type 2 diabetes are prone to limb osteomyelitis, a condition associated with high morbidity and mortality. The relationship between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use and outcomes in these patients remains unclear. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study using a large federated database from 2015 to 2024. Adult patients with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10 E11) and limb osteomyelitis were identified. GLP-1RA exposure was defined as use within 6 months prior to the diagnosis of osteomyelitis. Patients with end-stage renal disease, malignancy, or human immunodeficiency virus infection were excluded. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, amputation, sepsis, major adverse cardiovascular events, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury. Propensity score matching was applied to balance baseline characteristics and disease severity. Findings A total of 21,858 patients were identified. After propensity score matching, 2615 patients remained in each cohort with balanced baseline characteristics. GLP-1RA use was associated with lower mortality, with rates of 1.0% at 6 months (HR 0.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.30-0.78) and 4.7% at 3 years (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.78). title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Semaglutide in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease.
abstract: Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) increasingly develop type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, yet are excluded from cardiovascular outcome trials, and the effects of semaglutide here are unknown. Using the TriNetX Research Network, we conducted a retrospective new-user active-comparator study of adults with ACHD and T2DM initiating semaglutide (n = 2,385) or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor (n = 2,889) from December 2017 to December 2025. Cohorts were 1:1 propensity score matched, yielding 1,422 pairs followed for 3 years, with a sensitivity analysis matched on 27 lesion categories. Semaglutide was associated with lower all-cause mortality (7% vs 12%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51 to 0.85), hospitalization (40% vs 55%; HR 0.68, CI 0.61 to 0.76), and emergency department (ED) visits (35% vs 43%; HR 0.85, CI 0.75 to 0.96). Major adverse cardiovascular events (HR 0.71), heart failure (HR 0.74), and stroke (HR 0.65) were also lower; myocardial infarction and arrhythmia were not. Modulating Platelet Reactivity with GLP-1RAs in Diabetes: Mechanistic Insights, Potential Benefits, and Clinical Limitations in Atherothrombotic Prevention.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have redefined cardiovascular medicine, reducing major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) through pleiotropic mechanisms that transcend glycemic and weight control. While their cardioprotective benefits are well-established, their direct impact on platelet activity-a key driver of atherothrombotic risk-remains a compelling frontier. This narrative review first addresses the heightened atherothrombotic risk characteristic of patients with diabetes and the clinical challenges posed by their suboptimal response to standard antiplatelet regimens. Subsequently, it explores experimental evidence on the antiplatelet properties of GLP-1RAs. Mechanistically, GLP-1RAs exert a dual inhibitory action: direct modulation involves the activation of platelet-surface GLP-1 receptors, triggering the PKA signaling cascade and VASP phosphorylation, which in turn suppresses calcium mobilization and aggregation. Indirectly, these agents restore vascular health by enhancing nitric oxide bioavailability, preserving endothelial glycocalyx integrity, and shifting perivascular adipose tissue toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. Furthermore, GLP-1RAs mitigate the pro-thrombotic milieu by attenuating glycemic variability and systemic inflammatory cascades. Despite its undeniable effect on current society, it remains one of the diseases for which clinical trials have the highest failure rate, and therapeutic interventions remain palliative, thus creating an unmet demand to develop translational models that can accelerate pre-clinical drug discovery.ObjectiveWe aimed to develop a scalable neuronal phenotypic model using differentiated SH-SY5Y cells with mature neuronal phenotypes.MethodsSH-SY5Y were differentiated by exposure to either retinoic acid and phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate or retinoic acid and GLP-1. title: GNAZ regulates PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling, reversing sorafenib resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Background Sorafenib remains a treatment option for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, although acquired resistance limits its therapeutic efficacy. Guanine nucleotide-binding protein G (z) alpha subunit (GNAZ), a key mediator of cellular signal transduction, has been implicated in tumour progression and chemoresistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Herein, we sought to elucidate the functional role and underlying molecular mechanism of GNAZ in sorafenib resistance in HCC. Methods Bioinformatic analyses revealed the critical role of GNAZ in acquired sorafenib resistance in liver hepatocellular carcinoma. High GNAZ expression is significantly correlated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development, poor disease prognosis, and increased mutation burden. GNAZ silencing was conducted in sorafenib-resistant Huh7/S cells, followed by analyses of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and cellular phenotypes, including proliferation, migration, colony formation and apoptosis. In addition, the sensitivity of Huh7/S cells to sorafenib in combination with siGNAZ was evaluated. Results GNAZ knockdown attenuated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling, suppressed the proliferation, migration and colony-forming ability of Huh7/S cells, and promoted apoptosis. Combined treatment with GNAZ knockdown and sorafenib can increase the sensitivity of resistant Huh7/S cells to sorafenib. title: Targeting the IGF-estrogen receptor signaling nexus in thyroid cancer: From molecular crosstalk to precision therapeutics.
abstract: The potential convergence of insulin-like growth factor (IGF) and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) signaling represents a compelling molecular hypothesis in thyroid cancer, linking growth factor and hormonal responsiveness to malignant progression and therapeutic resistance. IGF signaling through IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R) and insulin receptor isoform A (IR-A) activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT-mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways, promoting proliferation and survival. An experimentally established IGF-2/IR-A autocrine loop further contributes to tumor-cell proliferation and impaired differentiation. Concurrently, ERα fosters proliferative and invasive phenotypes through keratin 19 (KRT19), potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 3 (KCNQ3)-associated MAPK activation, and epigenetic regulation, whereas estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) may exert context-dependent antiproliferative effects. Although reciprocal ERα-IGF-1R interactions have been demonstrated in non-thyroid models, direct molecular crosstalk in thyroid cancer remains unconfirmed. These findings provide a rationale for investigating ERα antagonism or degradation, selective ERβ activation, and IGF axis inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies. This article proposes that functional interplay between IGF and ERα signaling may create distinct oncogenic dependencies beyond the individual contributions of either pathway. title: Chronic Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: Microglial Autophagy, PI3K/Akt/mTOR Signaling, and Persistent Neuroinflammation.
abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major contributor to long-term disability and reduced quality of life after ischemic stroke, yet the mechanisms operating during its chronic phase remain insufficiently integrated. Increasing evidence suggests that, beyond the acute insult, dysfunction of the neurovascular unit and the blood-brain barrier, systemic immune responses, secondary neurodegeneration in distal brain regions, white matter degeneration, and structural disconnection of neural networks may all contribute to the development of PSCI, and the pathological consequences of these processes may persist into the subsequent subacute and chronic phases. Persistent neuroinflammation may contribute to these pathological processes and promote cognitive decline. Dysregulation of microglial autophagy and the class I phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling may represent candidate mechanisms underlying this persistent neuroinflammatory process. Under specific pathological conditions, sustained mTORC1 activity may promote inflammatory by inhibiting the initiation of autophagy and restricting the TFEB-dependent lysosomal transcriptional program, thereby impairing the clearance of damaged mitochondria and inflammation-related substrates. title: Lysosomes as multifunctional hubs of CD8+ T cell regulation.
abstract: Lysosomes have traditionally been recognized for their role in protein degradation. In CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs), most lysosomes represent a type of specialized lysosome-related organelle called a lytic granule (LG). LGs are comprised of lytic components, such as perforin (PRF1) and granzymes, that are required for the elimination of stressed, virus-infected or tumor cells. However, it is now well appreciated that lysosomes in CTLs have functions beyond cytotoxicity and serve as dynamic hubs for integrating signals driving cellular metabolism, mTORC1 signaling and autophagy. Together, this highly versatile organelle coordinates CTL activation, differentiation, memory formation and effector function. This Review examines the mechanisms by which lysosomes regulate LG biogenesis and secretion, autophagy, and metabolic reprogramming in CD8+ T cells. We additionally discuss how disruption of lysosomal pathways in CTLs impairs immune defense and contributes to immunodeficiency.
summary_short: Lysosomes have traditionally been recognized for their role in protein degradation. In CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs), most lysosomes represent a type of specialized lysosome-related organelle called a lytic granule (LG).

title: Tissue repair and regeneration: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic interventions.
abstract: Tissue injury is a pervasive feature of human disease, yet adult mammals exhibit limited regenerative capacity. A central determinant of regenerative outcomes is the inflammatory response, which orchestrates tissue repair through mechanisms that are evolutionarily conserved from Drosophila to mammals. Following injury, inflammation drives debris clearance, promotes the release of cytokines and growth factors, and contributes to the restoration of functional cells. However, dysregulated or unresolved inflammation can impair healing, drive scar formation, and ultimately result in organ dysfunction or failure. Here, we focus on recent advances in the spatiotemporal regulation of inflammation during tissue repair that have reshaped our understanding of its underlying mechanisms. We synthesize findings on the dynamic progression of repair from inflammatory initiation to active resolution and stem cell activation, highlighting features of immune cell plasticity and heterogeneity within injury-specific microenvironments, as well as the existence of pivotal macrophage-fibroblast interactions. Furthermore, we delineate the pleiotropic and context-dependent roles of key cytokines and signaling pathways in coordinating these processes. Finally, we discuss current and emerging therapeutic strategies, emphasizing the paradigm shift from broad immunosuppression toward precise modulation of inflammatory networks to promote regeneration and prevent fibrosis. A central determinant of regenerative outcomes is the inflammatory response, which orchestrates tissue repair through mechanisms that are evolutionarily conserved from Drosophila to mammals.

title: Metformin in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Aims To evaluate associations of metformin exposure with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and lactic or metabolic acidosis in adults with Type 2 diabetes and advanced CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 2 ) not receiving chronic dialysis. Materials and methods We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane from inception through 5 September 2026 for observational cohort studies evaluating metformin exposure in this population. Comparator strategies included non-use, discontinuation and alternative glucose-lowering therapy. Data were synthesized using Bayesian random-effects models with empirical heterogeneity priors (primary) and frequentist random-effects models. Certainty of the evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework. Results Ten cohort studies were included. For ESKD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) from the Bayesian analysis was 0.64 (95% CrI: 0.45-0.92; 99% posterior probability of HR Conclusions For ESKD, the pooled Bayesian estimate was below the null, whereas estimates for all-cause mortality and MACE remained uncertain, and an increased risk of acidosis could not be excluded. Given the very low certainty of the evidence and the heterogeneity of treatment strategies, these findings should be interpreted with considerable caution. Further randomized or well-designed observational evidence using clearly defined treatment strategies is needed.

title: Metabolic Profiles and insulin therapy requirements among pregnant women with Gestational Diabetes mellitus and Type 2 Diabetes across self-identified Race/ethnic groups in Brooklyn NY, USA.
abstract: Objective Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and type 2 diabetes (T2 DM) presents varying metabolic patterns across populations, yet the extent to which these differences appear at diagnosis remains unclear. This study examines whether baseline metabolic profiles differ among pregnant women from diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds. Our objective was to determine whether these metabolic differences may influence diabetes management during pregnancy. Study design We conducted a two‑year retrospective study of 200 insulin‑naïve women at NYU Langone hospital at Brooklyn, NY, diagnosed with GDM and or T2DM in the third trimester. The diagnostic criteria were standard two‑step testing , 50‑g glucose challenge (1Hr. GCT, cut off 135mg./DL) followed by a 100‑g Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). Baseline fasting labs included glucose, C‑peptide, and lipid profiles, with insulin sensitivity estimated using IS‑HOMA (C‑peptide). Management followed standardized diet, exercise, Metformin when appropriate, and weight‑based basal-bolus insulin titrated to fasting glucose levels 85-90 mg/dL and 2‑hour postprandial 115-120 mg/dL. Results Significant race/ethnicity‑specific metabolic phenotype differences emerged. Hispanic-Latina women and American born Black women had higher BMI, higher fasting C‑peptide, and lower insulin sensitivity, whereas Asian (Southeast and East Indian) and Caribbean/Haitian Black women showed lower C‑peptide but higher insulin sensitivity. title: Acute Hemolysis Due to Metformin in a Young Adult Treated for T-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
abstract: Background Patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) are at risk for hyperglycemia due to asparaginase, glucocorticoids, and possible underlying predisposition for glucose intolerance. The use of metformin in pediatric oncology patients is not yet widespread; however, it may be used to control blood glucose levels. Observation We report a young adult with T-cell ALL in maintenance chemotherapy who developed hemolysis 2 weeks after starting metformin, with resolution upon cessation of metformin. Conclusions We present this case to increase awareness of metformin-related hemolysis, review the literature, and discuss possible mechanisms for this adverse event.
