title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Survival in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Importance Metformin has known metabolic effects and associated survival benefits in head and neck cancer. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) also modulate systemic metabolism through regulating blood glucose levels and lipid metabolism. Objective To investigate whether GLP-1RAs are associated with survival outcomes in patients with head and neck cancers. Design, setting, and participants This retrospective cohort study was conducted using clinical data from January 1, 1990, through December 1, 2025, from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults with histologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC) were included. Data were analyzed in January 2026. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome was overall survival for all HNSCC and stratified by site. The secondary outcome was overall survival among patients concurrently using GLP-1RAs and metformin. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) with 95% CIs were estimated. Results There were 4532 patients (mean [SD] age, 63.4 [10.9] years; 1638 female individuals [36.1%] and 2891 male individuals [63.8%]) included in the cohort. Across all subsites, GLP-1RA users had significantly improved overall survival compared with controls at 1-year (aHR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.36-0.49), 3-year (aHR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.43-0.54), and 5-year intervals (aHR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.46-0.57). title: Beyond Bicarbonate: Renal Replacement Therapy in Refractory Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Introduction A minority of patients with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) remain profoundly acidaemic, despite receiving standard treatment as per established guidelines. This review examines the reported use of renal replacement therapy in that setting, proposes a working definition of refractory DKA, and sets out the differential diagnosis of persistent acidaemia that should be excluded before escalation is considered. Methods Targeted, purposive, non-systematic search of PubMed with citation tracking of retrieved articles. No protocol was registered, and no formal screening or risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken. The retrieval was not intended to be exhaustive, and completeness should not be inferred. Results To date, no clinical trial of bicarbonate has included patients with a pH below 6.85, although the current consensus permits its consideration below pH 7.0. Expert guidance on extra-renal purification exists for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, toxic alcohol poisoning, and salicylate toxicity; however, none addresses DKA. Reported cases document escalation for persistent acidaemia, yet circuit composition, anticoagulation, and insulin handling are infrequently recorded, and insulin clearance across a haemofilter has not been measured in this setting. Continuous therapy using glucose-free solutions has itself precipitated euglycaemic ketosis, including in people without diabetes. title: Train hard, recover smart: the supplement framework to enhance exercise recovery in recreational and elite-level athletes.
abstract: Background : Exercise-induced inflammation and muscle damage are frequent consequences of structured physical activity that facilitate muscle growth and subsequent training adaptations. Performance improvements are strongly dependent upon athletes' capacity to successfully recover from previous sessions or challenging efforts, particularly when opportunities to rest and recover are limited. Nutritional practices centered around acute or chronic ingestion of certain foods or dietary bioactive compounds have been shown to accelerate neurophysiological and subjective recovery outcomes and may be worthy of consideration in both recreationally active and professional athletic populations. Methods: This review provides a comprehensive summary of dietary strategies to promote exercise recovery that are supported by robust scientific evidence, including systematic reviews, randomized clinical trials, and observational studies up to August 2025. Results: Despite substantial variability in evidence quality, identified nutrients, dietary supplements, and bioactive compounds of greatest interest for athletes are omega-3 fatty acids and creatine monohydrate, while additional compounds showing promising results in improving subjective or objective recovery metrics such as inflammatory biomarkers, muscle soreness, and fatigue include magnesium, taurine, curcumin, L-Carnitine, Ashwagandha, anthocyanins, L-Citrulline, gingerol, tart cherry, beetroot, and pomegranate juice. title: Drinking behavior of feedlot Gyr heifers fed wheat silage as a replacement for corn silage.
abstract: Water is essential for maintenance, thermoregulation, digestion, and productive performance in cattle, and voluntary intake is strongly influenced by dry matter intake (DMI) and the diet's physical and chemical characteristics. This study evaluated drinking water intake (DWI), drinking visit frequency (DVF), water intake per visit (WI/V), and active time at the water trough (TWT) in feedlot Gyr heifers fed increasing proportions of wheat silage as a replacement for corn silage. Thirty-two heifers (357 ± 28.2 kg) were assigned to four treatments (n = 8/treatment, one pen/treatment) and received isonitrogenous diets (forage:​concentrate ≈ 80:20) with 0, 33, 67, and 100% replacement of corn silage with wheat silage. Daily data were analyzed using generalized linear mixed models (PROC GLIMMIX), with treatment, day, and temperature-humidity index (THI) as fixed effects and animal as a random effect. Mean THI was 75.0 (68.6 to 79.8). DMI did not differ among treatments (8.60 to 8.94 kg/d; P = 0.7178), and DWI, DVF, WI/V, TWT, and total water intake did not differ (P > 0.05). Under the conditions of this feedlot trial, replacing corn silage with wheat silage did not produce detectable changes in water intake or the heifers' drinking behavior; the results should not be extrapolated to lactating cows, grazing cattle, or severe heat-stress conditions.

title: An aging risk-factor scale: biomarkers of renal disease and anemia are primary predictors of three-year survival in common marmosets ( Callithrix jacchus )
abstract: Valid animal models are needed to evaluate how age-related changes in kidney function influence healthspan. Aging marmosets frequently develop renal insufficiency with anemia and exhibit reductions in body mass and metabolic rate. However, it remains unclear which age-related changes predict survival and which thresholds indicate increased mortality risk. We prospectively evaluated age, body composition, resting energy expenditure, hematology, and blood chemistry as predictors of 3-year survival in female and male marmosets ( n = 66), 2–16 years of age. Objectives were to identify prognostic markers, define high-risk thresholds, and to develop and test a composite risk-factor scale for mortality screening in captivity. A 10-variable model showed the best predictive performance in multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling, and was retained for further analysis (concordance = 0.881, p < 0.001). ROC curves using Youden’s Index and AUC identified high-risk thresholds for predictors in the multivariable model, and threshold-defined categories were evaluated by Kaplan–Meier survival analysis. The 10 binary risk-factors were combined into a composite scale scored from 0 to 10 and tested with Cox regression. The scale explained approximately 42% of variance in survival and each additional risk factor increased mortality risk 1.75-fold (95% CI: 1.43–2.14, p < 0.001). title: Longitudinal AI-based home-cage monitoring of locomotor aging in C57BL/6J mice: An exploratory pilot study
abstract: Aging is a multidimensional process characterized by progressive functional decline across physiological, cognitive, and behavioural domains. While home-cage monitoring systems (HCMS) offer unprecedented opportunities for continuous and non-invasive behavioural phenotyping, most existing applications rely on cross-sectional designs, limiting the ability to resolve longitudinal aging trajectories. Here, we present an exploratory pilot study based on continuous behavioural data acquired using the Digital Online Monitoring Equipment (DOME) AI-powered HCMS to characterize longitudinal aging trajectories in two partially overlapping cohorts of C57BL/6J mice. Twenty mice housed in four cages (four independent experimental units) were monitored for nine months each, together spanning 13 to 27 months of age. Cross-cohort concordance was explored within an overlapping window (19–21 months) to identify candidate behavioural features and assess potential cohort-specific bias. Among twenty extracted parameters, four locomotor kinematic measures (average movement acceleration, average overall speed, average speed when awake, and maximum movement speed) showed the highest cross-cohort concordance in both sexes in this exploratory screen and a consistent age-related decline. Because females exhibited consistently higher locomotor performance than males, sex-specific normalization was applied to account for sexual dimorphism while preserving longitudinal age-related patterns. title: Latent cortical network adaptability predicts dual-task–unmasked postural instability in Parkinson’s disease: a proof-of-concept study
abstract: Dual-task postural deterioration often reveals latent balance vulnerability in Parkinson’s disease (PD), even when single-task standing appears preserved. We examined whether beta-band cortical network solution-space organization during single-task standing predicts subsequent dual-task postural deterioration in PD. Forty-eight participants, including 16 healthy controls, 16 individuals with early-stage PD, and 16 individuals with mid-stage PD, completed single-task quiet standing and dual-task standing conditions while electroencephalography and center-of-pressure signals were recorded. Beta-band functional connectivity was estimated using the phase lag index, and minimum spanning tree (MST) analysis was extended using an iterative second-best MST framework to characterize alternative backbone configurations based on cumulative MST cost divergence from the optimal MST (Δ C total ( k )) and algebraic connectivity ( λ 2 ( k )). Dual-task-induced increases in postural sway became greater with advancing PD stage ( p = 0.008), whereas conventional MST metrics showed no significant disease-stage trends. In contrast, dual-task standing induced stage-dependent solution-space alterations, with early-stage PD showing reduced Δ C total ( k ) and increased λ 2 ( k ), suggesting a more constrained alternative backbone configuration. title: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity and functional disability in middle-aged and older adults: a harmonized multicohort study
abstract: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is highly prevalent in aging populations, yet its association and underlying mechanisms with functional disability (FD) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate CMM-FD relationship, quantify the influencing mechanisms, and explore heterogeneity across different CMM patterns and population subgroups. A multicohort study was conducted by pooling harmonized longitudinal data from three international aging cohorts. CMM was defined as the co-occurrence of at least two cardiometabolic diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, heart diseases, and stroke. FD was measured through difficulty performing basic or instrumental activities of daily living. Logistic regression models were used to estimate associations and heterogeneities, and Kohler-Holm-Breen decomposition was used to quantify mediating contributions. CMM prevalence was 22.53%, and FD prevalence was 23.01%. CMM was strongly associated with higher odds of FD (OR = 2.940; p < 0.001), with consistent findings across all countries and FD subtypes. Respiratory, neuropsychiatric, and sensory conditions jointly explained 20.44% of the association, with psychological problems contributing the largest share. CMM patterns involving stroke generally showed high odds of FD, while the four-disease combination had the largest overall point estimate. title: Impaired cellular stress adaptability in Alzheimer’s disease patient-derived fibroblasts: a PFKFB3-linked transcriptomic response to oxidative stress
abstract: Aging-related impairment in cellular stress adaptability may contribute to vulnerability to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but patient-derived experimental models that preserve agingassociated molecular features remain underused. Here, we investigated transcriptomic responses to oxidative stress in ex vivo dermal fibroblasts derived from patients with AD and control participants matched for age and sex. Fibroblasts were exposed to hydrogen peroxide to induce reactive oxygen species-mediated stress, followed by RNA sequencing to identify disease-associated differences in stress-responsive gene regulation. AD-derived fibroblasts exhibited distinct oxidative stress response patterns, with altered regulation of pathways related to endoplasmic reticulum stress, immune activation, autophagy, protein synthesis, and cell cycle control. Systematic candidate gene prioritization identified PFKFB3 as a key stress-responsive gene showing reduced induction in AD fibroblasts. Lower PFKFB3 responsiveness was associated with poorer cognitive performance and higher levels of neurodegeneration-related blood biomarkers, including plasma pTau217, neurofilament light chain, and glial fibrillary acidic protein. In immortalized human astrocytes, PFKFB3 knockdown reduced cell viability under oxidative stress and altered transcriptional programs related to proteostasis, metabolic regulation, and immune activation. title: Effect of multivitamin–mineral supplementation on cardiovascular-related functional health status in older adults: secondary findings from the COSMOS randomized clinical trial
abstract: Declines in cardiovascular-related functional health status are common with aging, yet the long-term effects of multivitamin–mineral (MVM) and cocoa extract (CE) supplementation on patient-reported outcomes remain unclear in older adults. This prespecified secondary analysis of the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) examined whether daily MVM or CE influenced Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores in generally healthy older adults and those with pre-existing heart conditions. COSMOS was a 2 × 2 factorial, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 21,442 US adults (men ≥ 60, women ≥ 65 years) without major cardiovascular disease at baseline. All participants were included in intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses of physical ability score (PAS), symptom burden (SB), and clinical summary score (CSS), representing KCCQ outcomes over 3 years. Linear mixed-effects models estimated treatment effects, with prespecified subgroup analyses among participants with cardiac conditions. Among a total cohort of over 21,000 participants, those taking a daily MVM versus placebo had small but statistically significant improvements in SB (MD 0.44, 95% CI 0.13–0.74) and CSS (MD 0.33, 95% CI 0.09–0.57) (both P < 0.05), with no significant effect on PAS, compared to placebo. title: Human mitochondrial DNA variants influence telomere length
abstract: Telomere shortening is a hallmark of aging, yet telomere length (TL) varies considerably between individuals and is strongly influenced by inheritance. In mice, efficient mitochondrial function and low reactive oxygen species (ROS) production are essential for telomere elongation during early embryogenesis. As mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes several subunits of the electron transport chain, we investigated whether mtDNA variants influence TL using a transmitochondrial cybrid model. Platelet-derived mitochondria from human donors with varying TL were introduced into mtDNA-depleted cells. Donor blood TL inversely correlated with cybrid ROS levels, suggesting that specific mtDNA variants may support telomere maintenance by enhancing mitochondrial fitness. During cybrid formation, a transient oxidative stress phase precedes cellular adaptation. At this stage, mtDNA variants associated with reduced complex I (CI) activity triggered rapid telomere shortening, which was rescued by antioxidant and NAD + precursor supplementation. Although these variants occur naturally in some individuals with long telomeres, our findings suggest that, under conditions of acute in vitro oxidative stress, CI activity is critical for preserving telomere integrity, potentially through the regulation of NAD + /NADH balance and PARP1 activity. title: Perspectives on healthy ageing: a qualitative study in Germany.
abstract: Background In response to population ageing, World Health Organization and United Nations launched the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing to promote well-being in older age through actions on ageism, age-friendly environments, integrated care and long-term care. In Germany, demographic ageing and healthcare fragmentation pose challenges, yet research exploring a collective understanding of these priorities remains limited. Methods This qualitative study involved twelve semi-structured interviews with older adults ( n = 6), healthcare professionals ( n = 4) and decisionmakers ( n = 2) in urban and suburban Central-West Germany. Participants were recruited through purposive and convenience sampling. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Ethical approval and informed consent were obtained. Findings Four themes were constructed. Participants linked healthy ageing to individual responsibility within fragmented welfare and healthcare structures. Age-friendly environments were described as contexts enabling continued meaningful living. Ageism was recognised across groups more than through personal experience. Integrated care was described as fragmented, particularly at home, with informal support filling care gaps. Conclusion Findings suggest that UN Decade priorities were reflected unevenly in participants' experiences. title: Toward standard testing methods in biophotovoltaics based on cyanobacteria.
abstract: Microbial biophotovoltaics (BPVs) are an emerging renewable energy technology that harnesses photosynthetic microorganisms to generate electric current. Despite the rapid growth of the field, the lack of standardized testing and reporting methods currently prevents the benchmarking of devices, slowing technological progress. This article provides a critical analysis of the experimental practices used in BPV research, highlighting the significant variability in device configurations, light sources, electrode materials, biomass quantification methods, and electrochemical measurement protocols reported in the literature. It further considers the historical standardization of protocols for conventional photovoltaics (PVs) and the resulting acceleration of the maturation and market adoption of PV technologies. Drawing inspiration from conventional PVs, the article outlines key steps toward BPV standardization, including defining common testing conditions, methods for data normalization, shared reference systems, and round-robin testing protocols. Establishing consensus in the testing protocols would significantly improve reproducibility and enable meaningful comparisons across laboratories, accelerating the development and deployment of BPVs.

title: The Maladaptive Stress State: A Systems Framework for Chronic Disease Persistence.
abstract: Chronic degenerative diseases are traditionally explained in terms of disease-specific initiating lesions and molecular pathways. Although this approach has substantially advanced understanding of disease mechanisms, it does not fully explain why biologically diverse disorders often converge on persistent states marked by chronic inflammation, impaired repair, altered nutrient sensing, reduced adaptive flexibility, and incomplete recovery after the initiating insult subsides. This Perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS), a systems-level framework that distinguishes disease initiation from persistence. Rather than proposing a new molecular pathway, the MSS framework integrates established knowledge from geroscience, stress biology, lysosomal signaling, nutrient sensing, and systems biology. It posits that chronic disease persists when adaptive stress programs become stabilized and the capacity to exit the stress-adapted state is impaired. Within this framework, systems-level interactions sustain evolutionarily conserved adaptive responses despite partial resolution of the original stressor. The framework also generates experimentally testable predictions and outlines translational implications for assessing therapeutic recovery through restored adaptive flexibility rather than normalization of isolated molecular biomarkers. title: Implantable sensors in modern healthcare: advances, clinical applications, and future directions.
abstract: Implantable sensors are emerging as powerful tools for continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and biochemical parameters, thus facilitating improved disease diagnosis, therapeutic monitoring, and personalized healthcare. Recent advances in microelectronics, materials science, and wireless technologies have accelerated the development of miniaturized implantable devices with enhanced sensitivity, biocompatibility, and long-term operational stability. This review outlines the fundamental principles and major categories of implantable sensors, including biochemical, electrophysiological, pressure, and temperature sensing systems. Particular attention is given to material selection, biointerface engineering, wireless communication, data processing, and integration with biological environments. Current applications in chronic disease management, cardiovascular monitoring, neuroengineering, and precision medicine are highlighted alongside key challenges related to biofouling, immune responses, power supply, device reliability, and data security. Ethical, regulatory, and clinical translation considerations are also examined. Finally, emerging trends in smart materials, self-powered platforms, and intelligent implantable systems are discussed, emphasizing their potential to advance next-generation healthcare technologies.
summary_short: Implantable sensors are emerging as powerful tools for continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and biochemical parameters, thus facilitating improved disease diagnosis, therapeutic monitoring, and personalized healthcare.

title: Beyond weight loss: GLP-1-based therapies and the reversal of type 2 diabetes pathophysiology.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D), producing substantial improvements in glycemic control and, with newer agents, unprecedented reductions in body weight. However, their effects extend beyond these conventional outcomes and include reductions in visceral and hepatic fat, improved insulin sensitivity, attenuation of glucolipotoxicity, and enhancement of β-cell function. These actions overlap with mechanisms implicated in the reversal of T2D following substantial weight loss, raising the possibility that GLP-1-based therapies may modify the underlying pathophysiology of the disease rather than simply control its metabolic manifestations. In this review, we integrate evidence linking ectopic fat accumulation, hepatic insulin resistance, altered lipid trafficking, oxidative and inflammatory stress, and β-cell dysfunction with the development and reversibility of T2D. We then examine how GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonism remodel these metabolic and cellular abnormalities and discuss whether such changes may facilitate β-cell functional recovery. Particular attention is given to the distinction between treatment-induced normoglycemia and medication-free remission. Although current evidence indicates that GLP-1-based therapies can profoundly modify the diabetic metabolic phenotype, durability after treatment withdrawal remains uncertain. title: General Practice Registrar-Led Community Lifestyle Medicine Group Consultations in Primary Care: A Quality Improvement Feasibility Evaluation.
abstract: Background Modifiable lifestyle behaviours are major drivers of chronic disease, particularly among older adults living with multimorbidity, yet scalable preventive models remain limited. Group consultations may offer a scalable route to preventive lifestyle support, but delivery depends on a primary-care workforce skilled in behaviour change and group facilitation. General practice (GP) registrar-led models that combine patient care with workforce development are not well described. Methods We conducted a single-arm, pre-post quality improvement feasibility evaluation of a GP-registrar-led programme across two north London boroughs in mid-2025. The intervention combined clinician physical activity training, multimodal recruitment through a GP, and a four-week community-based group consultation course (RESET) covering movement, nutrition, sleep, stress, habit formation, purpose, and social connection. Reach, baseline need, retention, direct cost, participant feedback, and exploratory pre-post self-reported outcomes were assessed descriptively. Results A total of 79 clinicians attended the training. Of the 149 patients who registered interest, 38 commenced the programme and 29 completed all four weeks (76% retention; 126 patient-sessions). Participants were older and high-need: mean age 64.1 years, 97% with at least one long-term condition, 68% multimorbid, 79% with a cardiometabolic condition, and only 21% meeting the aerobic activity guideline. title: When Clinical Innovation Outpaces Implementation: A Dual Diffusion Model for GLP-1 Therapy and Employer Cardiometabolic Health.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based and related incretin therapies have rapidly expanded from glycemic management to obesity and broader cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic care. Their population-health impact, however, depends on more than therapeutic efficacy. Translation into durable benefit requires clinicians to identify and manage appropriate patients, benefit systems to enable effective access, and patients to initiate and sustain treatment. This review applies diffusion of innovations theory to propose a dual diffusion model for GLP-1 therapy and employer cardiometabolic health. The model conceptualizes provider implementation and employer/plan effective access as interdependent organizational diffusion processes that converge on the patient treatment trajectory. Their interaction produces 4 implementation states: implementation failure, identification gap, access gap, and integrated opportunity. Employer/plan effective access is proposed as a construct extending beyond binary coverage to include eligibility, affordability, utilization management, provider access, administrative feasibility, continuity, and treatment-support infrastructure. The model further distinguishes treatment initiation from sustainability and introduces system-generated discontinuation as a conceptual description of treatment cessation driven by structural barriers. summary_short: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based and related incretin therapies have rapidly expanded from glycemic management to obesity and broader cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic care. Their population-health impact, however, depends on more than therapeutic efficacy.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Topic Whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use is associated with a lower risk of incident glaucoma or ocular hypertension (OHT) in adults, and whether the association differs by diabetes status or comparator. Clinical relevance Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, and every licensed treatment targets lowering intraocular pressure (IOP); none protects retinal ganglion cells directly. GLP-1RAs are widely prescribed and have been proposed to be neuroprotective, so whether this class of medication alters glaucoma risk matters at prescribing and to the search for pressure-independent treatment. Four earlier meta-analyses found no significant association but pooled non-equivalent comparators. Methods Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies, following PRISMA 2020 and registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251082642). PubMed was searched on 15 April 2026 and updated to 30 August 2026, with CENTRAL, Europe PMC, the first 100 Google Scholar results and bidirectional citation tracking as supplementary sources. Eligible studies were retrospective cohort or nested case-control studies of GLP-1RA exposure with incident glaucoma, OHT or IOP change as the outcome and with adjustment for confounding. Two reviewers screened, extracted and applied ROBINS-I. summary_short: Clinical relevance Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, and every licensed treatment targets lowering intraocular pressure (IOP); none protects retinal ganglion cells directly. Four earlier meta-analyses found no significant association but pooled non-equivalent comparators.

title: Association of Newer Glucose-Lowering Medications and Phenoconversion From REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder to Parkinsonian Disorders in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: It has been estimated that as many as 90% of patients with isolated REM behaviour disorder (iRBD) develop an α-synucleinopathy, yet there are currently no treatments proven to prevent or to delay phenoconversion. This study evaluated the association between glucose-lowering drug classes and incident Parkinson's disease (PD), parkinsonism, and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) among older adults with RBD and type 2 diabetes (T2D). We conducted a target trial emulation using a retrospective active-comparator new-user design with 2016-2020 Medicare fee-for-service claims data amongst beneficiaries ≥ 66 years with RBD and T2D and atleast 12 months of continuous enrollment before treatment initiation. We identified initators of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is). Patients with prior use of either drug during the 12-month baseline period or initiation of both drugs on the index date were excluded. Hazard ratios for incident PD, parkinsonism or DLB were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models with stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox proportional regression models with inverse probability of treatment weighting. A total of 148, 144 and 138 patients were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i, GLP-1RA versus SGLT-2i and SGLT-2i versus DPP-4i cohorts, respectively. Compared with DPP-4i use, GLP-1RA use was

Diquat Poisoning: Epidemiology, Molecular Mechanisms, Diagnosis, and Clinical Management.
abstract: Diquat (1,1'-ethylene-2,2'-bipyridinium dibromide) is a nonselective bipyridyl herbicide widely used in agriculture for crop desiccation and weed control. Following the global restriction of paraquat, diquat usage has surged substantially, leading to increased poisoning incidents particularly in agricultural regions of China and other developing countries, where intentional ingestion for self-harm constitutes the predominant exposure route with mortality rates of 16.7-60% depending on ingested dose and treatment timing. At the molecular level, diquat undergoes nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH)-dependent redox cycling generating excessive reactive oxygen species, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction, Nrf2-Keap1 pathway activation, and multiple regulated cell death modalities including apoptosis, necroptosis, and ferroptosis. However, a comprehensive synthesis integrating epidemiological patterns, molecular mechanisms, organ-specific pathophysiology, and evidence-based clinical management remains lacking. This review systematically examines the global epidemiology and demographic characteristics of diquat poisoning, elucidates the interconnected molecular pathways underlying multiorgan toxicity affecting kidneys, liver, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system, evaluates current diagnostic approaches including severity scoring systems and biomarker-guided prognostication, and critically appraises therapeutic strategies from emergency decontamination

title: Treatment outcomes and safety of oral β-blockers and sirolimus in children with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Objective To describe outcomes and safety of oral β-blockers and sirolimus in children with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE). Methods We retrospectively reviewed children with KHE receiving oral β-blockers or sirolimus at Beijing Children's Hospital from January 2016 to April 2026. Lesion regression at fixed time points, treatment duration, treatment discontinuation, recurrence, and safety were assessed. Results Thirteen patients received β-blockers and 11 sirolimus, including three with prior therapy. Baseline lesion measurements did not differ significantly, but the β-blocker group was younger [median 4.0 (IQR, 3.0-4.0) vs. 19.0 (10.5-29.5) months; p p = 0.038) and hyperhidrosis (0% vs. 54.5%; p = 0.003). Cumulative lesion-regression thresholds did not differ significantly through 9 months. At 9 months, >25%, >50%, and >75% regression occurred in 76.9%, 46.2%, and 23.1% with β-blockers versus 100.0%, 72.7%, and 18.2% with sirolimus, respectively. Treatment was discontinued in 9/13 and 3/11 patients (median durations, 40.0 and 18.0 months, respectively). No recurrence was observed after cessation. Safety events were reversible and manageable. Conclusions In this cohort, both treatments were associated with improvement, but baseline imbalances limit direct comparison. β-blocker responses in predominantly younger, less symptomatic patients require confirmation in larger prospective studies.
summary_short: Conclusions In this cohort, both treatments were associated with improvement, but baseline imbalances limit direct comparison. β-blocker responses in predominantly younger, less symptomatic patients require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Antibody-drug conjugates in HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer: evolving clinical roles and translational directions.
abstract: Rapid advances in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and an expanding clinical evidence base are reshaping treatment options for hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) metastatic breast cancer (mBC). Randomized trials have demonstrated progression-free survival benefits over chemotherapy for individual ADCs in defined populations, including settings before and after metastatic chemotherapy. As additional ADCs become available and indications expand, attention is increasingly focused on whether individual agents can improve outcomes over endocrine-based regimens in selected endocrine-eligible patients and on which therapies beyond conventional chemotherapy may retain activity after ADC progression. Addressing these questions requires integration of clinical evidence with a mechanistic understanding of ADC activity and resistance. In this review, we summarize selected mechanisms of ADC action and critically examine the evolving clinical roles of individual agents across settings defined by prior therapy. We also discuss treatment strategies after ADC exposure and resistance mechanisms relevant to target and payload selection. Finally, we review exploratory studies of candidate biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes, ADC-based combinations, and next-generation designs, highlighting their biological rationale, emerging evidence, and priorities for further evaluation.
summary_short: Finally, we review exploratory studies of candidate biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes, ADC-based combinations, and next-generation designs, highlighting their biological rationale, emerging evidence, and priorities for further evaluation.

title: Di/tripeptides in cancer: from mechanisms to therapeutics.
abstract: Research on tumor metabolic reprogramming has long centered on glucose, lipids and free amino acids. By contrast, di/tripeptides, which lie at the interface between protein breakdown products and functional metabolic signals, have only recently begun to be recognized as a distinct molecular tier in cancer biology. Compared with longer peptides, di/tripeptides display greater metabolic mobility and a clearer dependence on dedicated transport systems. Here we systematically review the sources, transport, metabolic use, biological functions and clinical translational potential of di/tripeptides in cancer. Current evidence indicates that di/tripeptides arise from endogenous protein degradation, dietary digestion and microbial metabolism. Under nutrient limitation, tumor cells can recover amino acids through carnosine dipeptidase 2 (CNDP2)-mediated extracellular cleavage of dipeptides or uptake of intact di/tripeptides followed by intracellular hydrolysis. Beyond their role as nutrient substrates, selected di/tripeptides directly influence tumor cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis and drug resistance, and shape the tumor microenvironment by modulating acid base balance, redox homeostasis, angiogenesis and immune cell function. At the clinical translational level, di/tripeptides have emerged as candidate metabolomic and peptidomic biomarkers, transporter targeted imaging probes, functionally modified therapeutic agents and engineered delivery modules. summary_short: Current evidence indicates that di/tripeptides arise from endogenous protein degradation, dietary digestion and microbial metabolism.

title: Mechanomedicine for Lung Transplantation: From Multiscale Forces to AI-Assisted Translation.
abstract: Long-term outcomes after lung transplantation remain limited by primary graft dysfunction and chronic lung allograft dysfunction, despite improvements in surgery, immunosuppression and infection control. Mechanical injury is a complementary contributor that remains insufficiently integrated into transplant care. The lung allograft must accommodate cyclic ventilation, reperfusion shear, thoracic constraints and matrix remodeling. These forces can disrupt the alveolar-capillary barrier, amplify inflammation and activate fibrotic programmes. Here we synthesize lung transplantation through a mechanomedicine framework that links organ-scale loading, cellular mechanotransduction and clinical decision-making. We discuss how computational models and artificial intelligence (AI) can integrate ex vivo lung perfusion waveforms, imaging-derived ventilation or strain patterns, and molecular injury markers to support graft-risk assessment. We then organize mechanotherapeutic strategies by clinical readiness, from protective ventilation, size matching and extracorporeal graft support to emerging interventions targeting mechanotransduction according to cell type and loading conditions. Finally, we outline a translational roadmap for standardized mechanical biomarkers, interpretable AI and clinician-supervised digital-twin models.
summary_short: Long-term outcomes after lung transplantation remain limited by primary graft dysfunction and chronic lung allograft dysfunction, despite improvements in surgery, immunosuppression and infection control. Mechanical injury is a complementary contributor that remains insufficiently integrated into transplant care.

title: Divider-Reservoir-Drain reconstruction after total gastrectomy: a two-patient technical case series with 30-day follow-up.
abstract: Following total gastrectomy, reconstruction must restore alimentary continuity while limiting reflux and impaired Roux-limb transit. We report Divider-Reservoir-Drain reconstruction in two non-consecutive men with locally advanced cardia adenocarcinoma. After D2 total gastrectomy, each reconstruction used a 25-mm esophagojejunostomy, an 8-10 × 3-4 cm jejunal reservoir, two diversion-to-Roux interfaces, and a 40-45 cm Roux limb. Operative time was 130 and 145 min, and blood loss was 50 and 80 ml. Oral intake began on postoperative days 7 and 6; hospital stays were 12 and 10 days. Neither patient had a complication, reintervention, or readmission within 30 days. In the fluoroscopic examination shown, contrast passed antegrade and the operator visually estimated about 80% emptying at 15 min. These two selected cases establish technical completion only. They do not support claims about durable reflux control, Roux stasis, or comparative safety.
summary_short: We report Divider-Reservoir-Drain reconstruction in two non-consecutive men with locally advanced cardia adenocarcinoma.

title: Allostatic load is not associated with augmented vasoconstrictive response to cold pressor test or functional sympatholysis in Black emerging adults.
abstract: Black individuals are disproportionately affected by hypertension (HTN), even after controlling for conventional risk factors (i.e., obesity, smoking, physical fitness). Emerging evidence implicates chronic psychosocial stress, including discrimination/race-related events, in HTN development. Allostatic load (AL) reflects the cumulative adverse impact of repeated activation of compensatory physiological responses to psychosocial stressors. We assessed the associations between AL and disruptions in vascular parameters that may indicate heightened HTN risk in Black emerging adults. Forearm blood flow (FBF) and vascular conductance (FVC) were measured during sympathoexcitation (cold pressor test; CPT), alone and with handgrip exercise, (EX + CPT) in 35 Black undergraduate students (24F/11M, 20 ± 1 years). AL was determined using both clinical cutoffs (AL-CC) and individual z-scores (AL-z) from nine biomarkers (heart rate, systolic blood pressure (BP), diastolic BP, C-reactive protein, glucose, creatinine, total cholesterol/HDL-C ratio, cortisol, %body fat). Higher scores reflected greater AL burden. AL scores were overall low (AL-z: 0.003 ± 3.9; AL-CC: 1.6 ± 1.2). Reductions in FBF and FVC during EX + CPT (∆FBF: -3.58% ± 3.14%; ∆FVC: -12.56% ± 6.77%) were significantly attenuated (P < 0.001) as compared to CPT alone (∆FBF: -24.15% ± 7.95%; ∆FVC: -35.54% ± 9.20%). summary_short: We assessed the associations between AL and disruptions in vascular parameters that may indicate heightened HTN risk in Black emerging adults.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors Versus Metformin as First-Line Therapy for Cardiorenal Outcomes: A Target Trial Emulation Among New Users With Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: Objective To compare cardiorenal and mortality outcomes associated with initiation of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors versus metformin as first-line glucose-lowering therapy among new users with type 2 diabetes. Patients and methods Using a target trial emulation design with TriNetX Global Collaborative Network data, we identified adults (≥18 years) with type 2 diabetes who were new users of SGLT2 inhibitors or metformin from January 1, 2018, through December 31, 2023, with follow-up through June 10, 2025. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary outcomes included individual MACE components, major adverse kidney events (MAKE), acute heart failure, all-cause mortality, and kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy. Propensity-score matching yielded 36,720 pairs. Results Over median follow-up of 2.5 and 3.5 years in the SGLT2 inhibitor and metformin groups, respectively, SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was associated with lower risks of MACE (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.84-0.92), all-cause mortality (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.68-0.77), stroke (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.79-0.90), cardiac arrest (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.95), and acute heart failure (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97). Myocardial infarction risk was similar between groups (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.91-1.04). title: Metformin Preserves Hippocampal and Prefrontal Synaptic Integrity in Rats with Spinal Cord Injury: SIRT1 Induction and microRNA Modulation.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is associated with memory-related behavioral deficits and dendritic alterations in supraspinal brain regions. We investigated whether metformin improves recognition-related behavior after SCI and examined accompanying structural and molecular changes. Adult female rats underwent clip-compression SCI and received daily intraperitoneal saline or metformin (50mg/kg) for 7 or 14 days; unoperated rats served as controls. Behavioral assessments included novel object recognition (NOR), Basso-Beattie-Bresnahan (BBB) locomotor scoring, and elevated plus maze (EPM) closed-arm-entry latency as an activity-related measure. Nissl and Golgi-Cox staining evaluated neuronal density and dendritic morphology in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex. Hippocampal gene expression and protein concentrations were assessed using quantitative PCR and ELISA. NOR acquisition indices were similar across groups, whereas NOR discrimination was lower in saline-treated SCI rats than in controls at both time points. Metformin increased NOR discrimination versus saline at 14 days (p < 0.0001), but not at 7 days, and improved BBB recovery in both cohorts (p < 0.0001). EPM closed-arm-entry latency was shorter with metformin at both time points (p < 0.001). summary_short: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is associated with memory-related behavioral deficits and dendritic alterations in supraspinal brain regions. Metformin increased NOR discrimination versus saline at 14 days (p < 0.0001), but not at 7 days, and improved BBB recovery in both cohorts (p < 0.0001).

title: Fermented <i>Laminaria japonica</i> ameliorates type 2 diabetes in mice <i>via</i> modulation of insulin signaling, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a global health challenge; therefore, safe and effective dietary interventions are required. We investigated the hypoglycemic effects of fermented Laminaria japonica in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, and elucidated the underlying mechanisms through integrated transcriptomic and gut microbiota analyses. Diabetic mice were orally administered fermented L. japonica , non-fermented L. japonica , or metformin for 4 weeks. Fermented L. japonica treatment significantly ameliorated hyperglycemia, improved insulin sensitivity, increased hepatic glycogen storage, and restored antioxidant enzyme (catalase, glutathione peroxidase, and total superoxide dismutase) activities compared to the NFS treatment. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that fermented L. japonica modulated key metabolic pathways, including PI3K-Akt signaling and AMPK activation, with upregulated gene expression associated with glucose metabolism ( Prkag3 and Tmem100 ) and oxidative stress response ( Ddit4 and Apod ). Additionally, 16S rRNA sequencing demonstrated that fermented L. japonica reshaped the gut microbiota by enriching beneficial short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa ( Limosilactobacillus and unclassified Lachnospiraceae) and suppressing potentially harmful genera. title: Astrocytes as a Convergence Point for Neuroprotection and Drug Repurposing in Long COVID Comorbidities.
abstract: Astrocytes are central regulators of metabolic homeostasis, redox balance, and neuroimmune signaling within the central nervous system, and accumulating evidence implicates these cells as key mediators of the neurological sequelae associated with long COVID. SARS-CoV-2 has been shown to infect neural cells, inducing substantial alterations in these regulatory parameters and promoting a sustained reactive astrocyte phenotype that compromises synaptic plasticity, blood-brain barrier integrity, and metabolic support, thereby contributing to neurometabolic and neuropsychiatric dysfunction. Despite the convergence of these findings, no review has addressed the interplay between astrocyte biology, systemic metabolic and psychiatric comorbidities, and the potential for drug repurposing within a gliopharmacological context in long COVID. In this review, we propose an astrocyte-centered model in which long COVID arises from the convergence of direct viral injury and pre-existing disorders. We then critically examine the repurposing potential of three pharmacological categories, each selected on the basis of their documented actions on astrocytic metabolic, redox, or inflammatory pathways: systemic medications already in wide clinical use for metabolic and cardiovascular indications, including metformin, angiotensin II receptor blockers, calcium-channel blockers, and statins; centrally acting agents with established or emerging use in psychiatry, such as selective serotonin reuptake in
summary_short: Astrocytes are central regulators of metabolic homeostasis, redox balance, and neuroimmune signaling within the central nervous system, and accumulating evidence implicates these cells as key mediators of the neurological sequelae associated with long COVID.

title: Imeglimin Protects Islets From Hypoxia via Mitochondrial Preservation and ROS Reduction, Improving Early Graft Survival.
abstract: Imeglimin is a metformin-derived antidiabetic drug that improves glycemia by optimizing mitochondrial function. Evidence suggests it enhances mitochondrial efficiency and preserves pancreatic β-cell mass (BCM) under diabetic stress. However, its protective effect against hypoxia-induced islet damage, a key cause of early β-cell loss after transplantation, remains unclear. We investigated the effect of imeglimin on hypoxia-induced mitochondrial dysfunction in islets and assessed its impact on an intramuscular islet transplantation model. Under 5% O2, imeglimin preserved mitochondrial membrane potential and normalized reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, whereas metformin alone failed to reduce ROS. Combined treatment showed complementary mitochondrial protection. Transcriptomic analysis identified restoration of Cox6a2 and attenuation of hypoxia-associated YAP/TAZ target gene signature. In vivo, imeglimin recipients showed improved glycemic control and glucose tolerance, and indium-111-labeled exendin-4 single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography confirmed greater graft BCM on day 14. Early graft histology revealed reduced apoptosis, oxidative stress marker presence, and HIF1A accumulation, alongside preserved TOMM20 and COX6A2 expression in the imeglimin group. title: Inositol for infertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
abstract: Rationale This is an update of a previously published review. Women with infertility may use adjunctive therapies to improve reproductive outcomes. Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are dietary supplements widely available and commonly used by women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS; renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in May 2026). The use of inositol for women with PCOS and infertility is based on proposed effects on insulin sensitivity and ovarian function. In clinical practice, myo-inositol is frequently prescribed for women with PCOS undergoing ovulation induction/intrauterine insemination or before in vitro fertilisation (IVF). However, the quality and certainty of the evidence supporting this practice remains unclear. This review aimed to assess the benefits and harms of inositol (including myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol) in women with PCOS experiencing infertility. Objectives To evaluate the benefits and harms of inositol oral supplementation for reproductive outcomes among women with polycystic ovary syndrome experiencing infertility. Search methods We searched CENTRAL (which includes trial registries), the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group Specialised Register, MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, AMED, and Epistemonikos to 10 November 2025. We also checked reference lists and contacted experts in the field for any additional trials. title: Weight-loss effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-age women with overweight or obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Background In reproductive-aged women with polycystic ovary syndrome, overweight or obesity exacerbates metabolic and reproductive risks; lifestyle interventions and metformin have limited weight-loss effects, and more effective pharmacological weight-loss strategies are urgently needed. The aim of this article is to evaluate the weight-loss and body-shape outcomes of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, and to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence. Methods Multiple databases and trial registry platforms were searched (2015.1-2025.12), and parallel RCTs in reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS comparing GLP-1 receptor agonists with non-GLP-1 regimens were included. The primary outcome was body weight change, secondary outcomes were BMI and waist circumference, and the exploratory outcome was visceral adiposity. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed, with effect sizes as mean difference or Hedges-corrected standardized mean difference, and RoB 2 and GRADE were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence. Results Five RCTs (N.=319) were included. Compared with controls, GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduced body weight (MD -2.80 kg, 95% CI: -3.94~-1.66), BMI (MD -1.02 kg/m 2 , 95% CI: -1.41~-0.62), and waist circumference (MD -3.53 cm, 95% CI: -4.63~-2.42), and sensitivity analyses showed consistent directions. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a potentially larger
summary_short: Compared with controls, GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduced body weight (MD -2.80 kg, 95% CI: -3.94~-1.66), BMI (MD -1.02 kg/m 2 , 95% CI: -1.41~-0.62), and waist circumference (MD -3.53 cm, 95% CI: -4.63~-2.42), and sensitivity analyses showed consistent directions.

title: Association of adverse perinatal outcomes of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy with maternal serum bile acid profiles.
abstract: Background Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is associated with increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, yet current monitoring lacks predictive accuracy. This study aimed to explore alterations in serum bile acid profiles and their relationship with adverse perinatal outcomes in ICP. Methods This study enrolled 149 pregnant women, including 77 normal pregnant women and 72 cases with ICP, subdivided into ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes and those without according to the perinatal outcomes. Serum concentrations of 15 bile acids were quantified using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry and compared among the three groups. Elevated levels of total bile acids and conjugated bile acids, including GCA, GCDCA, TCA, TCDCA, and TUDCA, were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes and might serve as candidate biomarkers for risk prediction. title: Circulating biomarkers in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma for risk stratification, diagnosis and prognosis.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to tumor heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and high recurrence rates even after curative treatment. Although HCC is potentially curable when detected at an early stage, suboptimal surveillance, particularly in patients with underlying cirrhosis or metabolic risk factors, limits the proportion of patients eligible for curative therapies. Current surveillance strategies for at-risk populations have intrinsic limitations, and the performance of imaging and serum biomarkers remains suboptimal. Moreover, the lack of reliable prognostic biomarkers for detecting early recurrence hampers post-treatment surveillance and impacts clinical outcomes. In this context, circulating biomarkers have emerged as promising tools for improving both early detection and prognostic stratification. Liquid biopsy has the potential to enable early, non-invasive diagnosis of HCC and allows longitudinal assessment of tumor progression through serial sampling. In early-stage HCC, blood candidates may complement or outperform conventional approaches by enabling earlier diagnosis and more accurate risk stratification. In this review, we summarize recent advances and current challenges in the clinical translation of circulating biomarkers. title: Circulating plasma taurine, GDF-15, and FGF-21 levels as candidate biomarkers of healthy aging.
abstract: Background Plasma taurine, Growth Differentiation Factor 15 (GDF-15), and Fibroblast Growth Factor 21 (FGF-21) have been proposed as blood-based biomarkers of biological age. However, their specificity for chronological age versus metabolic health requires further evaluation. Objective To evaluate whether plasma taurine, GDF-15, and FGF-21 concentrations differ between healthy young and older adults, and whether they correlate with metabolic health. Methods In a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis, overnight fasted plasma samples from 175 healthy young (18-35 y) and 137 older (64-89 y) adults were analysed for amino acids, taurine, GDF-15, and FGF-21. Associations with body composition and metabolic health were assessed using correlation analyses. Results Plasma taurine concentrations were lower in older than in young adults (144 [124-183] vs 169 [131-197] μmol/L, P=0.012) and correlated negatively with fat percentage (r s, adjusted =-0.141, P=0.018) and fasting glucose (r s, adjusted =-0.129, P=0.030), independent of age. GDF-15 and FGF-21 concentrations were higher in older adults (758 [618-1013] vs 275 [246-326] and 366 [184-578] vs 171 [82-356] pg/mL, respectively; both P 0.05), whereas FGF-21 correlated positively with BMI (r s, adjusted =0.180), fat percentage (r s, adjusted =0.351), fasting glucose (r s, adjusted =0.285), insulin (r s, adjusted =0.204) and HOMA-IR (r s, adjusted =0.241) (all P≤0.002). title: Maternal gestational crate confinement is associated with post-weaning behavioral differences and altered hippocampal molecular profiles in piglets.
abstract: We evaluated sow physiology, offspring behavior, and hippocampal molecular profiles under two gestational housing systems. Of 42 primiparous sows, 32 were group-housed (GP; 10 focal sows) and 10 were crated (CC). Maternal chewing was recorded on gestational d 25, 45, 65, 85, and 105; saliva was collected over d 21-25, 41-45, 61-65, 81-85, and 101-105 (cortisol, secretory IgA, and α-amylase), and serum on d 25, 45, 65, 85, and 105 (cortisol, interferon-γ, interleukin-6, dopamine, and brain-derived neurotrophic factor). Piglets (n = 16-18/group) underwent elevated plus-maze (d 28), restraint (d 32), open-field (d 35), and novel object (d 38-40) tests. Piglet serum (n = 10/group) was collected on d 28 (cortisol, IgA, interferon-γ, interleukin-6, dopamine, and brain-derived neurotrophic factor). On d 42, five brain regions (hippocampus, prefrontal cortex, hypothalamus, amygdala, and nucleus accumbens) were collected for biochemical analyses and quantitative real-time PCR. Hippocampal readouts included serotonin, β-endorphin, dopamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine, γ-aminobutyric acid, glycine, glutamate, taurine, and aspartate. Hippocampal tandem mass tag proteomics (n = 3/group), western blotting, and hippocampal/prefrontal histology and electron microscopy were performed. CC sows had more non-feeding chewing on d 45, 65, 85, and 105 (adjusted P 1.20 or < 1/1.20); 8 GO terms met FDR < 0.05 (complement activation, actin binding); KEGG suggested NF-κB and B-cell receptor pathways.
summary_short: We evaluated sow physiology, offspring behavior, and hippocampal molecular profiles under two gestational housing systems. Of 42 primiparous sows, 32 were group-housed (GP; 10 focal sows) and 10 were crated (CC).

title: Comet the bull, a historical genome from the agricultural revolution.
abstract: During the eighteenth century, new breeding practices reformed English farming, producing the Shorthorn breed, which grew to dominate English cattle herds. Comet (born 1804) was an early Shorthorn bull with such influence that he is referred to as the 'Adam' of the breed. He famously sold for 1000 guineas, and his breeding history influenced Sewall Wright in developing population genetic theory. From a curated tooth, we sequenced Comet's genome to high coverage (15.4×) and co-analysed it with published cattle genomes to assess his legacy on modern cattle. Almost half of Comet's genome consists of runs of homozygosity, validating his recorded pedigree and confirming the practice of extreme and deliberate in-and-in breeding at the inception of modern breeding. Despite the approximately 40 generations separating Comet from present-day Shorthorns, over half (58%) of his genome, identifiable through identity-by-descent (IBD) segments, segregates in present-day members of the breed. Shorthorns were internationally influential, and Comet also shares IBD with 17 other breeds included in our analysis. The genome regions that were transmitted to descendants with higher frequency harbour genes known to influence milk and meat production, immune system function and male fertility; Comet's genomic heritage may be associated with production traits selected for in the intervening centuries.

title: Adenosine deaminase co-immunization reverses age‑associated immunosenescence by restoring germinal center T follicular helper cell function
abstract: Older adults experience disproportionate morbidity and mortality from Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI); however, existing toxoid- and receptor binding domain (RBD)-based vaccines elicit suboptimal protection in aged hosts due to the age-associated defects in CD4 + T cell function, T follicular helper (T FH ) cell activation, and antibody quality. We evaluated whether adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzymatic immune modulator that degrades immunosuppressive adenosine, and improves GC T FH differentiation and survival, could reverse these age-related impairments when co-delivered with DNA vaccine plasmids targeting toxin A and B RBDs (pRBD). In aged mice, pRBD vaccination alone produced markedly reduced toxin-specific effector/memory CD4 + T cells, diminished T FH activation, and poor toxin A neutralization compared to vaccinated young mice. Co-immunization with plasmid-encoded adenosine deaminase-1 (pADA) restored toxin-specific CD4 + T cell generation and cytokine production, activation-induced marker (AIM) T FH responses, and antibody-mediate toxin neutralization to levels comparable to young adults. Mechanistically, pADA co-immunization was associated with the reduction of CXCR4 on germinal center (GC) T FH cells—a phenotype previously linked to impaired GC positioning and diminished B cell help in aging—suggesting that ADA may improve humoral quality through modulation of CXCR4 expression, a pathway previously associated with GC T FH positioning. title: Poor oral health, epigenetic aging, and mortality in older adults: a nationally representative follow-up study
abstract: Poor oral health may contribute to systemic aging-related pathophysiology through chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, but its relationship with molecular biomarkers of aging and subsequent mortality remains unclear. This prospective study investigated the associations of oral health with DNA methylation-based epigenetic age acceleration and evaluated whether it mediates the link between oral health and mortality. We analyzed data from 1,764 participants from the NHANES 1999–2000 and 2001–2002 cycles, linked to National Death Index mortality through Dec 31, 2019 (median follow-up: 17.4 years; IQR: 10.4–18.8). Periodontitis severity was classified as mild, moderate or severe using CDC/AAP definitions. Remaining teeth were categorized as ≥ 20, 10–19, 1–9, or edentulous. Seven epigenetic aging measures were examined: IEAA, EEAA, SBAA, PhenoAA, GrimAA, Grim2AA, and DunedinPoAm. Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear and Cox proportional hazards models, and mediation analyses were adjusted for sociodemographic, lifestyle, and anthropometric factors. Compared with participants without periodontitis, those with periodontitis exhibited accelerated epigenetic aging across all measures (β ranged 0.907–1.933; all P < 0.05). Participants with < 20 teeth had higher Grim2AA ( β = 1.188, P = 0.013) and GrimAA ( β = 1.083, P = 0.017). Associations tended to be stronger among males, drinkers, and smokers. title: No effect of post-meiotic sperm aging on male fertility in a species with finite sperm production
abstract: Post-meiotic sperm aging occurs when mature sperm cells are stored in the male reproductive tract before mating. In most species, males produce sperm throughout their life, thereby partially mitigating sperm aging by replenishing their sperm supply. By contrast, sperm production is finite in some species, preventing aging sperm to be replaced by new gametes. Finite sperm production is therefore predicted to impose strong selective pressure to minimize post-meiotic sperm aging. In this study, we tested this prediction by investigating post-meiotic sperm aging in a species with finite sperm production and pre-mating sperm storage in males, the buff-tailed bumblebee ( Bombus terrestris ). We adopted an integrative multi-level approach combining high-throughput flow cytometry, dual-type DNA methylation profiling, and untargeted proteomics. We identified molecular and cellular hallmarks of aging in sperm cells during male storage, including reduced sperm viability, elevated oxidative stress, increased DNA damage, and altered DNA methylation and proteomic profiles. However, these changes were modest in magnitude. Accordingly, neither male fertility nor reproductive fitness declined with age: males (hence, sperm) of different ages achieved similar mating success and sired colonies that did not differ in foundation success, productivity, composition, or lifespan, indicating that post-meiotic sperm aging has no significant impact on male reproductive performance. summary_short: We identified molecular and cellular hallmarks of aging in sperm cells during male storage, including reduced sperm viability, elevated oxidative stress, increased DNA damage, and altered DNA methylation and proteomic profiles.

title: Functional connectivity profile of the amygdala subfields associates with emotional well-being in aging
abstract: Amygdala-related functional connectivity (FC) plays a crucial role in human emotion, cognition, and mental well-being. The amygdala is a highly heterogeneous structure, with subregions that have both distinct and overlapping functions. However, the connectivity patterns of different amygdala subregions, and how these associations vary with age, remain poorly understood. Functional MRI data were analyzed from 68 younger adults and 66 older adults during movie watching in a 7-T MRI scanner. Partial least squares (PLS) analysis was used to identify latent variables capturing variance associated with age-related differences in the FC patterns of three amygdala subregions: the basolateral (BLA), centromedial (CMA), and superficial (SFA) nuclei. In addition, covariance between behavioral measures, including emotional resilience and cognitive function, and FC of these subregions were examined. We further explored correspondence with large-scale brain networks, the associated cognitive processes in Neurosynth, and the spatial distributions of neurotransmitter receptors of the identified connectivity patterns of the BLA, CMA, and SFA. Multivariate analyses revealed that functional connectivity patterns of amygdala subregions related to emotional resilience largely overlapped across widespread brain regions; however, their associations differed by age. title: Association of dietary essential amino acid intake profiles with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality
abstract: Dietary essential amino acids (EAAs) are crucial for metabolic health, but their association with long-term mortality remains unclear. Existing studies often focus on individual amino acids, failing to capture patterns of overall combined EAA intake.We analyzed data from two prospective cohort studies: the UK Biobank (UKB; n = 126,336) and the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES; n = 35,084). Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify distinct dietary EAA intake patterns. We examined the associations of these patterns with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality using Cox proportional hazards models and pooled the estimates via inverse-variance-weighted fixed-effects meta-analysis. Over a median follow-up of 14.2 years, 14,518 deaths were documented. Four distinct EAA intake profiles were identified: low, moderate, high, and very-high. Compared with the low-profile group, higher EAA intake profiles were associated with a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality in the pooled analysis (Moderate-profile: HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.83-0.92; High-profile: HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.78-0.90; Very-high-profile: HR = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.77-0.97). Similar protective associations were observed for cardiovascular and cancer mortality. title: New-onset depersonalization-derealization syndrome following semaglutide therapy.
abstract: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, acts on central neuropsychiatric pathways beyond its metabolic effects, yet dissociative adverse effects have rarely been reported. We describe a 42-year-old woman with no psychiatric history who developed recurrent, distressing episodes of depersonalization and derealization approximately 7 days after her second 0.5 mg weekly dose of semaglutide prescribed for obesity. The episodes progressed from once daily to 3 to 4 times daily over 10 days, with insight and reality testing preserved throughout. Metabolic, neurological, toxicological, and psychiatric evaluations, including brain imaging, electroencephalography, and laboratory studies, excluded alternative causes. She fulfilled the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition criteria for depersonalization-derealization disorder, and the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score of 6 indicated a probable causal relationship. Semaglutide was discontinued without psychotropic medication, and symptoms resolved completely within 4 weeks, with sustained remission at 3 months. This case suggests that depersonalization-derealization is an underrecognized, reversible neuropsychiatric adverse effect of semaglutide and underscores the need for clinician awareness and patient counseling during therapy.
summary_short: This case suggests that depersonalization-derealization is an underrecognized, reversible neuropsychiatric adverse effect of semaglutide and underscores the need for clinician awareness and patient counseling during therapy.

title: Successful hypertension control in 17-hydroxylase deficiency using crinecerfont.
abstract: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency (17OHD) is a rare form of CAH characterized by cortisol deficiency, impaired sex steroid production, and excess deoxycorticosterone (DOC), resulting in low-renin hypertension and hypokalemia. Management typically relies on glucocorticoid therapy to suppress adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-driven steroidogenesis, but adequate disease control may require supraphysiologic glucocorticoid doses and intensive antihypertensive treatment. Crinecerfont, a corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1) receptor antagonist approved for classic CAH, has not previously been reported in 17OHD. We describe a 23-year-old woman with 46,XY karyotype and classic 17OHD with severe persistent hypertension despite high-dose glucocorticoids, spironolactone, and multiple antihypertensive agents. Despite treatment escalation, DOC and pregnenolone levels remained elevated and blood pressure remained poorly controlled. Following initiation of crinecerfont 100 mg twice daily, blood pressure improved to 120-130/80-90 mmHg, plasma renin activity increased, and DOC and pregnenolone concentrations normalized without further glucocorticoid escalation. Clinical and biochemical improvements were sustained during 12 months of follow-up. title: Norepinephrine-dominant pheochromocytoma associated with impaired insulin secretion and insulin resistance.
abstract: Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) are known to cause impaired glucose tolerance through both impaired insulin secretion and insulin resistance driven by catecholamine excess. Previous experimental and clinical studies have suggested that noradrenergic PPGLs induce glucose intolerance predominantly through increased insulin resistance, whereas adrenergic PPGLs induce glucose intolerance primarily through impaired insulin secretion. We report a rare case of sporadic 123 I-metaiodobenzylguanidine-negative adrenal pheochromocytoma with a noradrenergic biochemical profile: while plasma norepinephrine and normetanephrine levels were elevated, plasma epinephrine and metanephrine levels were within the normal range. Detailed evaluation of glucose metabolism using a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test prior to surgery showed impaired early-phase insulin secretion, delayed peak insulin response, elevated fasting plasma glucose, and increased homeostasis model assessment for insulin resistance, while the test performed postoperatively, after tumor resection, showed improvement of all the above parameters, suggesting that both impaired insulin secretion and insulin resistance contributed to the glucose intolerance in this patient. title: Differences of sex development associated with asymmetric overgrowth in a patient with 69,XXY/46,XX mosaicism.
abstract: Individuals with both differences in sex development (DSD) and asymmetric overgrowth are rare. This clinical presentation may be associated with chromosomal mosaicism. Multiple methodologies may be needed to establish the diagnosis. An 11-month-old patient was referred for evaluation of DSD and segmental overgrowth. Clinical examination showed right-sided facial enlargement, predominantly left-sided limb overgrowth, macrodactyly, and hypo- and hyperpigmented skin lesions. Genital examination revealed clitoromegaly, a midline urogenital sinus, and a palpable right gonad. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a left-sided hemiuterus and a left intra-abdominal gonad. Gonadal biopsy revealed a dysgenetic testis on the right and an ovary on the left. Serum estradiol was 27 pg/mL (International System of Units [SI], 99.1 pmol/L) (reference range, 7-28 pg/mL [SI, 25.7-102.7 pmol/L]), consistent with female reference values. Post-human chorionic gonadotropin testosterone was 6.3 ng/mL (SI, 21.8 nmol/L) (reference value, >1 ng/mL [SI >3.4 nmol/L]), indicating functional testicular tissue. Peripheral blood karyotype was 46,XX, whereas a fibroblast culture obtained from skin biopsy demonstrated 69,XXY[6]/46,XX[34] mixoploidy. The SRY gene was absent in peripheral blood lymphocytes but was detected in the dysgenetic testis and skin fibroblasts. title: How We Use Corticosteroids in Immune Thrombocytopenia.
abstract: Introduction Corticosteroids remain an important first-line treatment for immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), but their benefits are accompanied by substantial toxicities across various body systems. Their use should therefore be individualised and time-limited. Methods We synthesise current guidance and published evidence concerning the selection of patients for corticosteroids treatment, choice of regimen, prevention and monitoring of treatment-related toxicity, recognition of response and non-response, and structured tapering and discontinuation in adults with ITP. Results Corticosteroids should be avoided when observation is clinically appropriate and, when prescribed, should have a pre-defined indication, haemostatic control target, expected time to response and stopping date. Accepted first-line regimens include prednisolone at 1-2 mg/kg/day, generally capped at 60-80 mg daily, or high-dose dexamethasone at 40 mg daily for 4 days. A platelet count exceeding 50 × 10 9 /L within 5-7 days generally identifies an early responder, although a lower count may be adequate when bleeding has resolved and haemostatic safety has been achieved. Responders receiving prednisolone should proceed to dose reduction and complete discontinuation within approximately 6-8 weeks. Patients without an adequate early response should have prednisolone tapered over approximately 2 weeks and with prompt consideration of an alternative or steroid-sparing treatment rather than prolonged dose escalation. summary_short: Introduction Corticosteroids remain an important first-line treatment for immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), but their benefits are accompanied by substantial toxicities across various body systems. Their use should therefore be individualised and time-limited.

title: Functioning gonadotropinomas with ovarian hyperstimulation and multicystic ovaries: a tale of 2 tumors and 2 organs.
abstract: Functioning gonadotropinomas are rare pituitary adenomas that secrete biologically active gonadotropins and may present with ovarian hyperstimulation and multicystic ovarian enlargement in premenopausal women, often mimicking primary ovarian disease and leading to delayed diagnosis. We describe 2 women with ovarian manifestations secondary to functioning gonadotropinomas. Case 1 was a 36-year-old woman who presented with a 12-year history of abnormal uterine bleeding and bilateral multicystic ovaries initially suspected to be ovarian neoplasms. Later, she developed progressive visual impairment in the right eye. Laboratory tests showed an elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level, and pituitary magnetic resonance imaging revealed a macroadenoma. Transsphenoidal surgery confirmed an FSH/luteinizing hormone-positive gonadotroph adenoma, with postoperative regression of ovarian cysts. Case 2 was a 28-year-old woman who presented with severe abdominal pain and bilateral multicystic ovaries complicated by ovarian torsion requiring unilateral ovariectomy and salpingectomy. Persistent ovarian enlargement with elevated gonadotropins and estradiol prompted endocrine evaluation, revealing a pituitary macroadenoma. Histopathology demonstrated FSH and steroidogenic factor 1-positive functioning gonadotropinoma.
